title: 第九章　改革共产主义一：赫鲁晓夫的莫斯科之春，1953—1964
originalTitle: 9 REFORM COMMUNISM I Khrushchev’s Moscow Spring, 1953-1964

children: 一个坏政府最危险的时刻，正是它开始改革自身的时候。
The most dangerous time for a bad government is when it starts to reform itself.
——亚历克西斯·德·托克维尔，论杜尔哥与路易十六
—Alexis de Tocqueville, anent Turgot and Louis XVI
我们害怕——真的害怕。我们怕解冻会引发洪水，我们控制不住，会把我们淹死。它怎么会淹死我们？它可能溢出苏联河床的两岸，形成巨浪，冲走我们社会的一切屏障和挡水墙。

We were scared—really scared. We were afraid the thaw might unleash a flood, which we wouldn’t be able to control and which could drown us. How could it drown us? It could have overflowed the banks of the Soviet riverbed and formed a tidal wave which would have washed away all the barriers and retaining walls of our society.
——尼基塔·赫鲁晓夫，谈1953年的权力交接
—Nikita Khrushchev, anent the changing of the guard in 1953

zh: 马雅可夫斯基关于列宁永驻苏联生活的说法，在1953年以后更适用于斯大林：尽管他在肉体上已不在人世，但他在精神上和政治上仍然活着，而且将继续活着，直到1991年制度终结。也可以毫不夸张地说，苏联历史余下的四十年将被一个压倒一切的问题所支配：如何埋葬斯大林。他的三位主要总书记继任者——赫鲁晓夫、勃列日涅夫和戈尔巴乔夫——主要关心的都是他的遗产所引发的问题。他们的政策要么是为了修正和改革这份遗产，要么是为了保护和保存它；更确切地说，这些政策在两种关切之间来回摇摆。但无论走哪条路，制度的问题都只是愈发严重。因此，三位领导人都以失败离场，并留下了一场新的危机。
en: Maiakovskii’s words about Lenin’s eternal presence in Soviet life are even more applicable to Stalin after 1953: Although he no longer lived physically, he still lived, and would continue to live, both morally and politically, until the end of the system in 1991. It is also no exaggeration to say that the remaining four decades of Soviet history would be dominated by one overriding problem: How to bury Stalin. All three of his principal successors as General Secretary—Khrushchev, Brezhnev, and Gorbachev—were primarily concerned with the problems engendered by his legacy. All of their policies were devised either to amend and reform it, or to protect and preserve it; or, more exactly, these policies oscillated between the one and the other concern. But whichever tack was followed, the problems of the system were only aggravated. Thus all three leaders departed the scene in failure and bequeathed a legacy of new crisis.

zh: 因此，斯大林之后的苏联历史，标志着在斯大林统治下那段漫长的表面稳定期之后，战时共产主义与新经济政策之间、即“强硬”列宁主义与“温和”列宁主义之间交替的恢复——这种交替曾是十月革命后最初十二年的特征。这出不断重演的两幕剧如今将继续下去：赫鲁晓夫治下是新经济政策为期十年的弱化了的重演，勃列日涅夫治下是长达十八年的常规化战时共产主义或新斯大林主义，最后是戈尔巴乔夫治下为期六年、短暂却失控的新经济政策。然而，这些苏维埃主义基本阶段看似永恒的复归，并不可能真正重复第一个周期，因为那个周期在1929年以前就已完成。
en: So Soviet history after Stalin marks the resumption, after the long period of apparent stability during his reign, of that alternation between War Communism and the NEP, or between “hard” and “soft” Leninism, that had characterized the first twelve years after October. The drama in two acts constantly repeated would now continue, with a muted replay of the NEP for a decade under Khrushchev, then a routinized War Communism or neo-Stalinism for eighteen years under Brezhnev, and finally a brief but runaway NEP for six years under Gorbachev. Yet these seemingly eternal returns to the basic moments of Sovietism could not really be repetitions of the first cycle, which was completed before 1929.

zh: 勃列日涅夫常规化的新斯大林主义，只是原版的苍白复制品：真品在制度史上只能出现一次，因为斯大林主义正是在建设社会主义的那一刻产生的。只有这一革命性突破的过程，才能为斯大林规模的强制提供正当理由，因为斯大林主义并不像人们常常以为的那样仅仅是强制性恐怖：它是为了实现社会主义突破而施行的恐怖。同样，在斯大林将战时共产主义制度化二十五年之后出现的“新经济政策”，不可能等同于最初那版临时而短命的战时共产主义之后的新经济政策。列宁的战时共产主义在失败中崩溃，只留下制度的骨架供党日后使用；斯大林的战时共产主义则是一种“成功”，因为它造就了堆积如山、顽固难移的制度群，而且这些制度又因军事胜利和国际强权地位而获得神圣光环，被“个人崇拜”所神圣化。因此，斯大林主义是苏联历史自十月以来一直朝着它攀升的顶峰，而在1953年后的四十年里，历史将从这个顶峰缓慢下行。
en: The routinized neo-Stalinism of Brezhnev was a pallid replica of the original: the real article could occur only once in the system’s history because Stalinism was generated by the very moment of building socialism. Only this process of revolutionary breakthrough could justify coercion on a Stalinist scale, for Stalinism was not just coercive terror, as is too often assumed: it was terror to achieve the socialist breakthrough. Similarly, a “NEP” after Stalin’s institutionalized quarter century of War Communism could not be the same as a NEP after the improvised and ephemeral first version of War Communism. Lenin’s War Communism had collapsed in failure, leaving only a skeleton of institutions for the Party’s future use; Stalin’s War Communism was a “success” in the sense that it created a mountainous and resistant mass of institutions that was consecrated, moreover, by military victory and international power, and that was sacralized by the “cult.” Thus Stalinism was the peak towards which Soviet history had been building since October, and from which it would slowly descend in the four decades after 1953.

zh: 因此，这第二个下降周期中的新经济政策式改革，最好另起一个名称：“改革共产主义”。改革共产主义应被理解为一种努力：在不放弃其完整社会主义性质——即计划、集体所有制和党的领导作用——的前提下，使斯大林主义的遗产人道化和自由化。改革共产主义的奠基之父赫鲁晓夫把自己的纲领称为回归“真正的列宁主义原则”。他的对手则称之为“修正主义”，这或许是原初列宁主义词汇中最严重的罪名。他的拥护者回答说，这些怀旧的斯大林主义者是“教条主义者”。改革共产主义的另一个经典名称，是1968年捷克斯洛伐克的口号“人道面孔的社会主义”。还有一个名称是铁托元帅的“社会主义自我管理”。邓小平把他的版本称为“四个现代化”。但改革共产主义或许最著名的名称，是戈尔巴乔夫的“改革”（
）。正如这些例子所示，这一现象并非苏联俄国独有，而是一旦社会主义建成，就会出现在所有共产主义制度中。这些例子也表明，每一案例的侧重点都有所不同，取决于该国的背景以及改革尝试所处的共产主义阶段。尽管如此，所有这些尝试都有某些共同特征。
en: The neo-NEPs of this second, descending cycle, therefore, are best given the separate designation “Reform Communism.” And Reform Communism is to be understood as an effort to humanize and liberalize the Stalinist legacy without abandoning its integral socialist nature, that is to say, planning, collective property, and the leading role of the Party. The founding father of Reform Communism, Khrushchev, called his program a return to “true Leninist principles.” His adversaries called it “revisionism,” perhaps the worst sin in the original Leninist vocabulary. His adherents replied that these nostalgic Stalinists were “dogmatists.” Another classic name for Reform Communism is the Czech slogan of 1968, “socialism with a human face.” Still another name is Marshal Tito’s “socialist self-management.” Deng Xiaping called his version the “four modernizations.” But perhaps the most famous name for Reform Communism is Gorbachev’s “

.” As these examples indicate, the phenomenon is not unique to Soviet Russia but occurs in all Communist systems once socialism has been built. As these examples also indicate, the emphasis in each case is somewhat different, depending on the nation’s background and the stage of Communism at which the reform effort is attempted. Nonetheless, all of these attempts have certain characteristics in common.

zh: 这些特征是由改革共产主义所针对的斯大林主义秩序的性质所决定的。这种性质可以概括为：社会生活统一于一个权力中心。只有一个领袖、一种真传、一条“正确”的政策路线，以及一个无所不包的制度——党，它通过其下属机构即计划、警察和军队来运作。而这个一元的社会主义世界被视为始终在同外部资本主义敌人作斗争。这至少是该制度的理论和抱负；在斯大林最后的岁月里，这在俄国、东欧、中国，以及稍后的古巴和越南，都离现实相去不远。改革共产主义制定纲领的方式，就是试图软化这一制度，同时不破坏社会主义社会所必需的精神上与功能上的统一。
en: These characteristics are dictated by the nature of the Stalinist order against which Reform Communism is directed. This nature may be summarized as the unity of life in one center of authority. There is one leader, one true teaching, one “correct” line of policy, and one all-embracing institution, the Party, operating through its subinstitutions: the Plan, the police, and the military. And this unitary socialist world is seen as being in constant struggle with the external capitalist enemy. This, at least, is the theory and the aspiration of the system; and during Stalin’s last years it was not far from the reality in Russia, Eastern Europe, China, and, slightly later, in Cuba and Vietnam. Reform Communism developed its program by attempting to soften this system without destroying the moral and functional unity necessary to socialist society.

zh: 改革共产主义这一通用纲领的第一个要素，是努力讲出斯大林主义或毛泽东主义过去的一部分真相，削弱“谎言”，复兴批判性思考，以改善制度的运转；这不可避免地意味着总体上一定程度的文化与思想自由化。第二个要素是经济上的分权化，以提高效率和增进民众的物质福利。第三个要素与第二个相关：它要为个人和企业设计激励，使他们愿意工作、生产和盈利，同时仍然不放弃计划而转向市场。最后一个要素是国际缓和，即放松那些使共产主义制度长期处于被围困和内部动员状态的紧张关系。第一个尝试改革共产主义纲领的国家，正是该制度的发源地俄国；而鉴于苏联模式在各地共产主义合法性中的首要地位，俄国制度的危机只能意味着改革共产主义将在整个国际运动中扩散。
en: The first element in the generic program of Reform Communism is an effort to tell a part of the truth about the Stalinist or Maoist past, to attenuate the Lie and revive critical thought in order to improve the workings of the system; and this inevitably means some measure of general cultural and intellectual liberalization. The second element is an effort at economic decentralization in order to promote greater efficiency and the material well-being of the population. The third element is related to the second: it consists of devising incentives for individuals and enterprises to work, produce, and make a profit while still not abandoning the Plan in favor of the market. And the final element is international détente, the relaxation of those tensions that maintain Communist systems in a permanent state of siege and internal mobilization. The first country to try the program of Reform Communism was that of the system’s origin, Russia; and given the primacy of the Soviet model for the legitimation of Communisms everywhere, the crisis of the system in Russia could only mean the spread of Reform Communism throughout the whole international movement.

zh: 去斯大林化
en: DE-STALINIZATION

zh: 改革共产主义出现的第一个名称是“去斯大林化”，因为整个运动始于拆除已故领袖个人独裁的机器。斯大林死后，原政治局（此时称主席团）立即恢复了1937年以前的权力，党的半宪法也以“集体领导”的名义重新激活。在这个统治集团内部，权力起初似乎落入了莫洛托夫、贝利亚和马林科夫三人之手；而马林科夫作为斯大林在十九大指定的继承人，成为政府首脑。赫鲁晓夫被同僚低估，得到了他们以为次要的职位——党的第一书记，而斯大林在执政生涯末期曾把这个职位置于其总理角色之下。统治集团的所有成员都明白，局势充满危险，因此必须向民众作出让步；甚至连贝利亚也成了自由化的倡导者。
en: The first term to emerge for Reform Communism was “de-Stalinization,” for the whole movement began with the dismantling of the machinery of the late Leader’s personal dictatorship. Immediately after his death the old Politburo, now called the Presidium, was restored to its pre-1937 authority, and the semiconstitution of the-Party was reactivated under the name “collective leadership.” Within this ruling group power at first seemed to pass to a triumvirate of Molotov, Beria, and Malenkov; and the latter, as Stalin’s designated heir at the Nineteenth Party Congress, became head of the government. Khrushchev, underestimated by his colleagues, received what they thought was the secondary post of First Secretary of the Party, a position that Stalin had subordinated to his role as prime minister at the end of his career. All members of the ruling group understood that the situation was fraught with danger and that concessions to the population were therefore imperative; even Beria became an advocate of liberalization.

zh: 然而，在同僚们看来，贝利亚及其警察正是任何此类自由化的主要障碍。他显然渴望独自掌权，而且在安全机关中拥有这样做的手段。对贝利亚来说，更大的不利在于：1937年以后，斯大林是通过警察来统治党的；因此，任何制度改革的第一步，都是再次把警察置于党之下。于是，赫鲁晓夫主动组织同僚们推翻贝利亚。6月，在莫斯科和柏林战役的英雄朱可夫元帅帮助下，贝利亚在一次政治局会议上被捕；他受到秘密审判，并于12月被处决。这将是最后一次出于政治原因对一位重要人物使用死刑。与此同时，国家安全部被降格为国家安全委员会，即克格勃，并隶属于部长会议。这向官名录和广大民众发出了信号：大规模恐怖已经结束，党如今是国家中的最高权力。
en: To his colleagues, however, Beria and his police were the principal obstacles to any such liberalization. He clearly aspired to take power on his own, and he had, in the security organs, the means to do so. An even bigger liability for Beria was the fact that after 1937 Stalin had ruled the Party through the police; so the first step in any reform of the system was to subordinate the police to the Party once again. Accordingly, Khrushchev took the initiative in organizing his colleagues for Beria’s overthrow. Beria was arrested at a Politburo meeting in June, with the aid of Marshal Zhukov, the hero of the battles of Moscow and Berlin; he was tried in secret and executed in December. This would be the last time the death penalty was used against a major figure for political reasons. At the same time, the Ministry of State Security was downgraded to a Committee of State Security, or KGB, and subordinated to the Council of Ministers. This was a signal to the
and to the population at large that the mass terror had ended and that the Party was now supreme in the country.

zh: 但是，改革当然不可能止于寡头集团的这一自卫行动；恐怖的终结唤醒了全国的期望，而这些期望很快便有了自己的势头。知识分子的自由化期望曾在战后被“日丹诺夫运动”击碎，此时他们怯生生地表达了对制度普遍放松的希望，用伊利亚·爱伦堡一部平庸小说的标题来说，就是“解冻”。当时不那么显眼但更重要的是，斯大林的死，尤其是贝利亚的垮台，动摇了古拉格的旧秩序。劳改营被暴动震撼，暴动严重到必须由军队镇压。
领导层很快意识到，古拉格在政治上和经济上都已经代价太高，难以维持；它必须被撤销，数百万囚犯必须获释。与此同时，死去的和活着的泽克的亲属纷纷涌向政府，要求平反。
en: But reform, of course, could not stop with this act of self-defense by the oligarchy; the end of the terror awakened expectations throughout the country that soon acquired a momentum of their own. The intellectuals, whose expectations of liberalization after the war had been dashed by the

, now timidly voiced hopes for a general relaxation of the system, a “thaw,” to quote the title of a mediocre novel by Ilia Ehrenburg. Less visibly at the time but more importantly, the death of Stalin, and especially the fall of Beria, undermined the old order in the Gulag. The camps were shaken by revolts so severe that they had to be put down by the army.

The leadership soon realized that the Gulag had become too costly politically and economically to preserve; it would have to be liquidated and its several million inmates released. At the same time, the relatives of the
who were dead as well as of those who were alive deluged the government with demands for rehabilitation.

〔译注〕诺里尔斯克劳改营起义始于1953年5月，早于贝利亚同年6月被捕；各次起义的具体背景并不完全相同。

zh: 正是在这样的背景下，赫鲁晓夫在1956年第二十次党代表大会上的“秘密报告”中直接攻击斯大林。
他有若干动机。其中之一无疑是成为最高领袖的个人野心。1955年，赫鲁晓夫已经迫使马林科夫辞去总理职务，由自己的盟友尼古拉·布尔加宁接替。攻击斯大林会败坏莫洛托夫、卡冈诺维奇等斯大林主义元老的名声，并可能将他们清除，从而巩固自己对党的控制。另一个可能的动机——赫鲁晓夫的崇拜者这样断言——是基本的人道良知，以及他对斯大林所犯罪行的真诚厌恶。
还有一个动机是严酷的必然性：随着数百万泽克返乡，真相很快就会暴露；因此最好主动应对这一发展，而且是按照党自己的条件来应对。
en: It is against this background that Khrushchev moved to attack Stalin directly in his “secret speech” at the Twentieth Party Congress in 1956.

He had a number of motives. One, no doubt, was his personal ambition to become supreme leader. In 1955 Khrushchev had already forced Malenkov’s resignation as prime minister and his replacement by his own ally, Nikolai Bulganin. An attack on Stalin would discredit and possibly eliminate such old-guard Stalinists as Molotov and Kaganovich, and thereby consolidate his own hold over the Party. Another possible motive, as Khrushchev’s admirers assert, was a basic human decency and his genuine revulsion at the crimes Stalin had committed.
Still another was the harsh necessity born of the fact that, with several million
returning home, the truth would soon out; it was thus best to anticipate this development, and to do so on the Party’s own terms.

zh: 但还有一个动机，也许是最根本的，尽管它与前三个动机并不矛盾。尽管多年来一直是斯大林俯首听命的工具，赫鲁晓夫仍然真诚信仰他青年时代的列宁主义，信仰那种把社会主义视为“光辉未来”的意识形态承诺——而斯大林曾试图通过清洗，用对当下他本人“崇拜”的盲目服从取代这一承诺。这种态度的一个原因，是赫鲁晓夫在领导层中的代际位置。与莫洛托夫和卡冈诺维奇不同，他年纪不够大，未能在内战期间成为斯大林的亲信，因而也未能在“大攻势”期间成为将军；而与勃列日涅夫不同，他又不够年轻，不完全是斯大林主义制度的产物。他也不是党的中央书记处那种纯粹的党务机器官僚，不像与他年龄相近的马林科夫。正如我们所见，他在内战期间只是党的一名普通士兵，在“大攻势”中也不过是一名中尉。此外，他职业生涯的大部分时间都在外地的党的队伍中度过，基本远离莫斯科，贴近工人和农民的实际问题。
en: But there was yet another motive, perhaps the most fundamental, though it is by no means incompatible with the first three. For all his years as Stalin’s pliant instrument, Khrushchev had remained a true believer in the Leninism of his youth, in that ideological commitment to socialism as the “radiant future” that Stalin had attempted to replace, through the purges, with blind obedience to his own “cult” in the present. One reason for this attitude was Khrushchev’s generational position within the leadership. Unlike Molotov and Kaganovich, he was not old enough to have become one of Stalin’s henchmen during the Civil War, and thus a general during the Great Offensive; and unlike Brezhnev, he was not young enough to be entirely a product of the Stalinist system. Nor was he a pure apparatchik of the Party’s central Secretariat, as was his near contemporary, Malenkov. He had been, as we have seen, only a Party foot soldier during the Civil War and no more than a lieutenant in the Great Offensive. Moreover, most of his career had been spent with the Party troops in the field, largely away from Moscow and close to the practical problems of workers and peasants.

zh: 对赫鲁晓夫这一代人来说，革命的神秘魅力始终非常真实，尽管这一事实并没有使他在赤裸裸的权力操纵上比其他列宁主义者逊色。他如何把自己对革命理想的忠诚，与他在清洗高峰时期于莫斯科和乌克兰为斯大林密切效劳的事实调和起来，我们不得而知。他自称对真实情况在很大程度上并不知情；然而，尽管他比莫洛托夫或卡冈诺维奇卷入得不那么直接，他不可能不知道基本真相。他大概靠布尔什维克的老原则“反对党的人不可能正确”熬过了那些年，但在当时，斯大林
党——而斯大林是个非常危险的人。无论如何，斯大林一死，赫鲁晓夫的目标就是清除党内斯大林主义的
，即“歪曲”，使党回归真正的列宁主义原则。
en: For Khrushchev’s generation the mystique of the Revolution was always very real, although this fact did not render him any less adept than other Leninists at the raw manipulation of power. How he reconciled his commitment to the ideals of the Revolution with his close service to Stalin at the height of the purges, both in Moscow and in Ukraine, we do not know. He claimed for himself a large measure of ignorance of the true state of affairs; yet, although he was less directly involved than Molotov or Kaganovich, he could not have helped but know the basic truth. He probably got through those years by resorting to the usual Bolshevik principle “you can’t be right against the Party,” but at the time Stalin
the Party—and Stalin was a very dangerous man. In any event, once Stalin was gone, Khrushchev’s aim was to purge the Party of Stalinist
, or “distortions,” and return it to its true Leninist principles.

zh: 因此，赫鲁晓夫以自己的方式想成为“当代列宁”（尽管他没有使用这个口号），成为最终让制度实现人的潜能和经济潜能的领袖。他的抱负是准备从已经实现的“社会主义”过渡到完整的“共产主义”——自马克思《哥达纲领批判》以来，这一直被视为无产阶级专政发展历程的既定方案。同样，他想释放制度的创造潜力，以最终证明它优于“资本主义”。正是这种令人振奋的前景，而不是某种可怕的威胁，才是赫鲁晓夫1959年对惊恐的美国主人夸口“我们要埋葬你们”时，以及向他们许诺他们的“孙子将在共产主义下生活”时所想到的。也正是出于这些原因，他想摆脱斯大林主义的老近卫，成为唯一的最高领袖。
en: Thus, in his own way, Khrushchev wanted to be the “Lenin of his day” (although he did not use that slogan), the leader who would at last permit the system to realize its human and economic potential. His ambition was to prepare the transition from the “socialism” that had already been achieved to the full “communism” that had been the scenario for the life history of the proletarian dictatorship ever since Marx’s

. By the same token, he wanted to release the system’s creative potential in order to demonstrate definitively its superiority over “capitalism.” It is this uplifting prospect, and not some dire threat, that Khrushchev had in mind when he boasted to his alarmed American hosts in 1959—“we will bury you”—and when he promised them that their “grandchildren will live under Communism.” And it is for these reasons that he wanted to get rid of the Stalinist old guard and become the sole supreme leader.

〔译注〕“我们要埋葬你们”广为人知的发表场合是1956年在莫斯科波兰使馆的接待会；1959年访美期间美国人士又提及这句话。“你们的孙辈将生活在共产主义下”另有访美时的当事人转述。

zh: 正是在这种混合动机的驱使下，赫鲁晓夫迫使政治局同僚就范，并利用斯大林死后的第一次代表大会发动了去斯大林化。这无疑是赫鲁晓夫一生中做过的最重要的事情；而其结果也像他的动机一样复杂。一方面，苏联民众获得了近十年的前进与希望，这是该国自新经济政策以来所经历过的最好时期，也是直到“公开性”之前的最好时期。另一方面，由于斯大林崇拜在国内制度和世界共产主义运动中都处于核心地位，赫鲁晓夫对这位已故领袖的攻击，开始拆散维系整个结构的神话之线。
en: It is with this mix of motives that Khrushchev forced the hands of his Politburo colleagues and used the first post-Stalin Congress to launch de-Stalinization. This was no doubt the most important thing Khrushchev ever did; and the results were as mixed as his motives. On the one hand, the Soviet populations were given nearly a decade of forward movement and hope, and the best period the country had known since the NEP, or that it would know until

. On the other hand, since the cult of Stalin was so central to both the internal system and the world Communist movement, Khrushchev’s attack on the departed leader began to unravel the threads of myth that held the whole structure together.

zh: 但这场讲话只是开启了这个过程，因为它远未对过去和盘托出：赫鲁晓夫只谴责了斯大林的某些罪行，而且只谴责那些针对党的罪行，并且只限于1936年以后。尽管如此，苏联权力的首脑如今已承认，在苏联权力的核心存在犯罪活动，因此这一事实再也不能被当作资产阶级的诽谤而置之不理。讲话内容在全国广泛流传，并在国外全文发表——赫鲁晓夫若预料不到这一切，就太天真了。自《莫洛托夫—里宾特洛甫条约》以来，莫斯科还从未抛出过这样的重磅炸弹。国内外许多信徒的信仰动摇了；另一些信徒以及人民阵线的道德继承者则断定，斯大林只是一个“反常”，苏联可能正在开始向社会民主主义过渡。诚然，四个月后，在苏联斯大林主义者和外国共产党领导人的双重压力下，中央委员会发表了一项决议，试图限制损害：斯大林被宣布为伟大的“理论家和组织者”，是“社会主义胜利”的缔造者，他的功绩只是因性格缺陷导致的某些滥用权力行为而蒙上污点。然而，“崇拜”已无法真正恢复；其有害后果立即在制度最薄弱的环节——东欧——显现出来。
en: But the speech only began this process, for it by no means made a clean breast of the past: Khrushchev denounced only some of Stalin’s crimes, and at that, only those committed against the Party and only after 1936. Nonetheless, the head of Soviet power had now admitted that criminal activity had existed at the heart of Soviet power, so this fact could no longer be dismissed as a bourgeois calumny. The contents of the speech became widely known throughout the country, and it was published in full abroad—all of which Khrushchev would have been naive not to expect. There had been no such bombshell out of Moscow since the Molotov-Ribbentrop Pact. Many of the faithful, both at home and abroad, were shaken in their faith; others of the faithful, as well as the moral heirs of the Popular Front, concluded that Stalin had been only an “aberration,” and that the Soviet Union might be beginning a transition to social democracy. True, four months later, under pressure of both Soviet Stalinists and foreign Communist leaders, the Central Committee published a resolution attempting to limit the damage: Stalin was declared a great “theorist and organizer,” the author of the “victory of socialism,” whose record was marred only by certain abuses of power due to flaws in his character. Still, the “cult” could not really be restored; and the deleterious consequences of this immediately made themselves felt at the system’s weakest link, Eastern Europe.

children: 〔译注〕秘密报告确以党内受害者为重点，但也批评了对整个民族的强制迁徙，因此并非只谈针对党员的罪行。
〔译注〕秘密报告确以党内受害者为重点，但也批评了对整个民族的强制迁徙，因此并非只谈针对党员的罪行。

zh: 原因并不难找。东欧的斯大林主义只有不到十年的历史，而不是二十五年；工人们仍然记得一个更多元的秩序——在某些国家还记得社会民主主义——有些地方的农民尚未完全集体化。但也许最重要的是，共产主义被视为外来势力强加的不合法制度。事实上，麻烦在斯大林死后立即就开始了：1953年，捷克斯洛伐克的比尔森发生了骚乱，东柏林则发生了一场真正的工人起义——由提高工厂生产定额引发——不得不由苏联坦克镇压。秘密报告把东欧的不稳定推向了高潮。
en: The reasons for this are not far to seek. Stalinism in Eastern Europe was less than a decade, not twenty-five years, old; the workers still remembered a more pluralistic order—and in some countries, social democracy—and in places the peasants were not yet fully collectivized. But perhaps most important of all, Communism was experienced as an illegitimate foreign imposition. Indeed, trouble had begun immediately after Stalin’s death: In 1953 there were riots in Pilsen in Czechoslovakia, and there was a genuine workers’ insurrection—triggered by the raising of factory production norms—in East Berlin that had to be put down by Soviet tanks. The secret speech brought Eastern European instability to its climax.

zh: 危机始于最大也最不安分的卫星国波兰。

导火索是6月波兹南的工人暴动，这次暴动同样被坦克镇压。不满很快蔓延为全国性的，1954年获释的哥穆尔卡此时作为改革派候选人出现，准备领导党。这一前景令莫斯科大为惊恐，于是赫鲁晓夫在老近卫莫洛托夫和卡冈诺维奇的陪同下，于10月飞抵华沙加以阻止——必要时动用罗科索夫斯基的军队。但哥穆尔卡威胁要以武力保卫华沙，而不是退让，因此让步的是苏联人。罗科索夫斯基被撤职，赫鲁晓夫接受了“通往社会主义的不同道路”原则，以换取哥穆尔卡对无产阶级国际主义的忠诚承诺。在实践中，波兰的“民族共产主义”意味着完全自治、结束集体化，以及天主教会的广泛自主。作为回报，自治只能在党的领导下、并在严格忠于苏联同盟的前提下行使。于是，波兰局势稳定了十年，成为改革共产主义取得部分成功的少数案例之一。但波兰的十月帮助触发了匈牙利类似危机的悲剧结局。
en: The crisis began in the largest and most restive satellite, Poland.

The spark was a labor revolt in Poznan in June that was again put down by tanks. Discontent soon became national, and Gomulka, who had been released from prison in 1954, now emerged as the reform candidate to head the Party. This prospect so alarmed Moscow that Khrushchev, flanked by the old guardists Molotov and Kaganovich, flew into Warsaw in October to head it off—if necessary with Rokossovski’s army. But Gomulka threatened to defend Warsaw by arms rather than back down, so it was the Soviets who gave way. Rokossovski was removed, and Khrushchev accepted the principle of “different roads to socialism” in exchange for Gomulka’s pledge of loyalty to proletarian internationalism. In practice, Poland’s “national Communism” meant full home rule, the end to collectivization, and broad autonomy for the Catholic Church. In return, home rule was to be exercised only under the leading role of the Party and in strict fidelity to the Soviet alliance. And so the Polish situation was stabilized for a decade in one of the few cases of a half-way successful Reform Communism. But the Polish October helped trigger a tragic outcome to a similar crisis in Hungary.

zh: 匈牙利的工人、知识分子和民族不满力量与波兰大致相同，但那里没有一个既能代表他们、又能约束他们，从而赢得苏联信任的哥穆尔卡。

匈牙利解冻开始时，令人憎恨的总书记拉科西违背赫鲁晓夫自己的政策，选择了镇压。莫斯科于是介入，用几乎同样强硬的埃尔诺·格罗取代拉科西，此举只会使局势进一步激进化。莫斯科随后又派出其备用改革共产主义者伊姆雷·纳吉，但为时已晚，因为此时波兰的先例已经触发了要求结束俄国占领的大规模街头示威。在这种压力下，纳吉与非共产党党派组成联合政府，从而放弃了党的领导作用；最后，他要求撤走苏联军队，并让匈牙利退出华沙条约组织。
en: The forces of worker, intelligentsia, and national dissatisfaction in Hungary were roughly the same as in Poland, but there was no Gomulka who could represent and at the same time restrain them, and thereby gain the confidence of the Soviets.

When the Hungarian thaw began, the hated General Secretary Rakosi opted for repression, contrary to Khrushchev’s own policy. Moscow then intervened and replaced Rakosi with the almost equally hard-line Ernö Gerö, a move that only radicalized the situation further. Moscow then put in its reserve Reform Communist, Imre Nagy, but too late, for now the Polish example had triggered large street demonstrations demanding the end of Russian occupation. Under this pressure, Nagy created a coalition government with non-Communist parties, thereby abandoning the leading role of
Party; and he ended by demanding the withdrawal of Soviet troops and taking Hungary out of the Warsaw Pact.

zh: 纳吉因此违反了东欧共产主义制度所赖以立足的两项原则。因此，莫斯科若要继续做莫斯科，就别无选择，只能干预。尽管这次干预显然不是赫鲁晓夫的首选政策，但他一旦决定，就毫不犹豫地用坦克碾碎布达佩斯，随后处决纳吉——这完全符合列宁在喀琅施塔得行动的传统。赫鲁晓夫还断然扶植了一个新政府，由先前曾被拉科西监禁的领导人亚诺什·卡达尔领导。他的使命首先是恢复共产党的控制，其次是在纳吉所违反的两项根本原则的限度内改革制度。假以时日，卡达尔的努力将带来比波兰更成功、并暂时稳定的改革共产主义（它将持续到1989年）。
en: Nagy thus violated the two principles on which the Communist system in Eastern Europe rested. Moscow accordingly had no alternative but to intervene if it were to remain Moscow. And although this intervention was obviously not Khrushchev’s first choice of policy, once he had made it he did not hesitate to crush Budapest with tanks, and later to execute Nagy—quite in the tradition of Lenin’s action at Kronstadt. Khrushchev also summarily installed a new government under a leader recently imprisoned by Rakosi, Janos Kadar. His mission was, first, to restore Communist control and, next, to reform the system within the limits of the two cardinal principles Nagy had violated. In time, Kadar’s efforts would lead to an even more successful and temporarily stable Reform Communism (it was to last until 1989) than the one in Poland.

zh: 但在这两个案例中，都没有建立起真正可行的秩序，因为两个政权的生存都依赖于对苏联和地方党的一定程度的顺从，而这种顺从剥夺了它们的国家合法性。在斯大林治下，苏联在东欧的帝国之所以脆弱，是因为它建立在无法无限期维持的强制和集中控制水平之上，1956年的“十月革命”就证明了这一点。在这些动荡和对“通往社会主义的不同道路”的承认之后，东欧帝国仍然脆弱，因为它此时依赖于当地民众的自愿合作；而他们之所以给予合作，只是因为他们害怕不顺从会招致莫斯科的报复——这种局面只能在莫斯科仍有能力强迫合作时维持。因此，总的来说，1956年的改革削弱了集团的凝聚力。与此同时，苏联国内的改革反对者也获得了一个有力的论据，用来反对赫鲁晓夫在国内的政策——以及反对他本人。
en: But in neither case had a genuinely viable order been created, since the survival of both regimes depended on a degree of submission to the Soviets and to the local Party that deprived them of national legitimacy. Under Stalin the Soviet empire in Eastern Europe had been fragile because it rested on a level of coercion and centralized control that could not be maintained indefinitely, as the “October Revolutions” of 1956 demonstrated. After these explosions and the recognition of “different roads to socialism,” the East European empire still remained fragile because it now depended on the willing collaboration of the local populations; yet they accorded this only because they feared Moscow’s reprisals if they did not—a situation that could last only so long as Moscow retained the capacity to compel collaboration. Thus, on balance, the cohesion of the bloc had been weakened by the reforms of 1956. At the same time, the opponents of reform in the Soviet Union had been given a great argument against Khrushchev’s policies at home—and against his person.

zh: 在苏联国内，秘密报告所激起的反响远不如东欧那样爆炸性，但它确实催生了知识分子异见的开端。1956年，E. N. 布尔贾洛夫等历史学家在一系列文章中，超越了赫鲁晓夫对苏联过去的谨慎重新审视，开始从根本上拆解《简明教程》的工作，从1917年讲起；布尔贾洛夫随即被解职。更重要的是，鲍里斯·帕斯捷尔纳克在《日瓦戈医生》中对革命进行了重新评价，近乎谴责。
当手稿被苏联刊物《新世界》拒绝后，帕斯捷尔纳克于1957年在国外出版，从而开创了“萨米兹达特”的伟大传统。该书被译成所有主要语言，立刻成为世界畅销书；1958年，帕斯捷尔纳克被授予诺贝尔奖。莫斯科的丑闻极其巨大；帕斯捷尔纳克被迫拒绝该奖，作家协会的大多数同僚也被迫谴责他。尽管如此，事实已经证明，解冻在俄国也可能失控，正如它在东欧一样。
en: Within the Soviet Union the secret speech provoked nothing so explosive as what happened in Eastern Europe, but it did produce the beginnings of dissidence among the intellectuals. In 1956 historians such as E. N. Burdzhalov, in a series of articles, went beyond Khrushchev’s circumspect reexamination of the Soviet past and began to fundamentally undo the work of the
, beginning with 1917; Burdzhalov thereupon was fired. Even more important, Boris Pasternak in
undertook a reevaluation of the Revolution that came close to being a condemnation.
When the manuscript was turned down by the Soviet review
, Pasternak had it published abroad in 1957, thereby inaugurating the great tradition of

. Translated into all major languages, it instantly became a worldwide best-seller, and in 1958 Pasternak was awarded the Nobel Prize, The scandal in Moscow was immense; Pasternak was forced to decline the prize, and most of his colleagues in the Writers’ Union were forced to condemn him. Still, it had been demonstrated that the thaw could get out of hand in Russia, just as it had in Eastern Europe.

zh: 秘密报告还有另一个负面后果：与中国裂痕的开端，以及随之而来的“国际工人运动”的衰落。

把世界共产主义运动维系在一起的，只有斯大林个人的权威；他的世界历史性成功，使任何对他领导地位的挑战对除铁托以外的所有共产党首领都不可想象。但听命于马林科夫和赫鲁晓夫之流则是另一回事，对中国尤其如此，因为中国自己的领袖毛泽东此时已是国际运动中最资深的英雄。因此，在斯大林之后的形势下，中国方面希望得到平等伙伴的待遇。于是，赫鲁晓夫未与他们商量就采取如此重要的步骤——把共产主义的核心偶像斯大林拉下神坛——令他们愤怒。此外，中国人对苏联还有一些更实际的怨恨，尤其是涉及满洲的怨恨，可以追溯到斯大林时代。因此，他们把捍卫斯大林、反对赫鲁晓夫的“修正主义”，当作对苏联表明独立、乃至意识形态优越的手段。这还不是公开决裂，但已经是一场破坏性的拉锯战。
en: There was yet another negative consequence of the secret speech; the beginning of the rift with China and the consequent decline of the “international workers’ movement.”

It was only Stalin’s personal authority that had held the world Communist movement together; and his world-historical success made any challenge to his leadership inconceivable to all Communist chiefs except Tito. But deferring to the likes of Malenkov and Khrushchev was quite another matter, especially for the Chinese, whose own leader, Mao, was now the senior hero of the international movement. In the post-Stalin situation, therefore, the Chinese wished to be treated as equals and partners. Hence they were outraged by Khrushchev’s taking so important a step as the desacralization of Communism’s central icon, Stalin, without consulting them. In addition, the Chinese had their more practical grievances against the Soviets, especially over Manchuria, going back to Stalin’s time. They therefore took the defense of Stalin against Khrushchev’s “revisionism” as a means for asserting their independence, indeed their ideological superiority, vis à-vis the Soviets. This was not yet an open break, but it was already a disruptive tug-of-war.

zh: 莫斯科新领导层的罪过，又因赫鲁晓夫的另一项创新而加重：他向头号修正主义者铁托示好。
1955年，赫鲁晓夫前往贝尔格莱德，实际上向南斯拉夫人道歉，希望把他们拉回“社会主义阵营”；这可以看作他天真的列宁主义在国际主义上的一种反映。南斯拉夫人当然不打算重回阵营，但他们利用苏联承认他们确实是“社会主义国家”，作为对其正在进行的工人“自我管理”实验的认可。
en: The sins of the new Moscow leadership were aggravated by another of Khrushchev’s innovations: his overtures to the archrevisionist, Tito.

In 1955 Khrushchev went to Belgrade and in effect apologized to the Yugoslavs in the hope of bringing them back into the “socialist camp”; this may be counted an internationalist reflection of his naive Leninism. The Yugoslavs, of course, were not about to rejoin the camp, but they used the Soviet recognition that theirs was indeed a “socialist country” as a sign of approval of their ongoing experiment in workers’ “self-management.”

zh: 事实上，铁托此时正忙于设计他自己那一套改革共产主义。

与中国一样，南斯拉夫人也是通过照搬现成的斯大林模式来启动社会主义的。然而到1950年代初，为了证明他们与莫斯科决裂有理，他们开始阐发一种替代性的社会模式，铁托有时称之为“现实社会主义”——多年以后，勃列日涅夫以截然相反的含义使用了这个说法。对南斯拉夫人来说，这个口号意味着莫斯科那一套社会主义并非真品；因此铁托提议把权力从中央集权的党国下放到民众自我管理机关——这是对最初俄国革命的苏维埃和“公社国家”的呼应。具体而言，这种更民主的南斯拉夫社会主义意味着：第一，放弃集体农庄，代之以普通合作社；第二，由选举产生的工人委员会管理工业；第三，为国家六个以民族为基础的共和国建立联邦结构。旧制度中唯一保留的集中化要素是党（此时重新命名为共产主义者联盟）及其军队。
en: In fact, Tito was now engaged in devising his own brand of Reform Communism.

Like the Chinese, the Yugoslavs had launched their socialism by taking over the ready-made Stalin model. By the early 1950s, however, in order to justify their break with Moscow, they began to elaborate an alternative model of society that Tito on occasion called “real socialism”—an expression Brezhnev used years later in a diametrically opposite meaning. For the Yugoslavs, this slogan meant that Moscow’s brand of socialism was not the genuine article; so Tito proposed to devolve power from the centralized Party-state to popular organs of self-management—an echo of the soviets and the “commune state” of the original Russian Revolution. Concretely, this more democratic Yugoslav socialism meant: first, the abandonment of the collective farm for ordinary cooperatives; second, elected workers’ councils for the management of industry; and third, a federal structure for the country’s six ethnically based republics. The only centralized element of the old system that was retained was the Party (now rebaptized League of Communists) together with its army.

zh: 但这已足以确保改革的民主要素失败。这里不妨先说说后来的情况：尽管农民大体上自行其是，工人委员会很快又落回党的控制之下，联邦制则把经济分割成互不协调的片段，却没有给六个地区共和国带来真正的自治。结果是经济受地方党而非中央党的控制，发展速度滞后，对西方的依赖日益加深——旅游业和输出“东方劳工”（
）——无论国家享有多少繁荣。而联邦制只有在那位富有魅力而专横的元帅还在世、能把他的王国维系在一起时才起作用。虽然这段时间非常长，因为他活到1980年，但仍不足以让南斯拉夫的改革共产主义转变为宪政秩序、真正的市场经济或真正的联邦。因为铁托激进的改革共产主义，并不比赫鲁晓夫较为犹豫的版本更能打破党国的模子；当终结到来时，它是崩溃，而不是转型。
en: But this was quite enough to insure that the democratic elements of the reform would fail. To anticipate a bit, although the peasants largely went their own way, the workers’ councils soon fell back under the control of the Party, and federalism divided the economy into uncoordinated segments without bringing genuine autonomy to the six regional republics. The result was local rather than central Party control over the economy, a lagging rate of development, and increasing dependence on the West—tourism and the export of

—whatever prosperity the country enjoyed. And federalism worked only so long as the charismatic and despotic marshal was there to hold his realm together. Although this turned out to be a very long time because he lived until 1980, it was not long enough for Yugoslav Reform Communism to transform itself into a constitutionalist order or a genuine market economy or a real federation. For Tito’s radical Reform Communism, no less than Khrushchev’s more hesitant version, failed to break the mold of the Party-state; and when the end came, it did so as a crash, not a transition.

〔译注〕原文将战后赴西欧工作的人员称为 Ostarbeiter；该词也特指二战期间被纳粹德国强征的“东方劳工”，两者的历史处境不能混同。

zh: 此外，在1950年代，赫鲁晓夫与铁托和解的努力并没有给苏联改革带来多少好处。诚然，1956年铁托预先认可了赫鲁晓夫镇压匈牙利分离行动是保卫社会主义所必需的，尽管他后来批评镇压过于严厉。但他绝不会重新加入“阵营”，反而与尼赫鲁、纳赛尔和苏加诺一起成为“不结盟运动”的创始人，该运动旨在成为国际事务中介于北约和苏联集团之间的第三种力量。尽管这股不结盟力量更偏向东方而非西方，南斯拉夫政权因其独立和自我管理社会主义，仍然为苏联的东欧卫星国树立了一个坏榜样。最后，南斯拉夫仍是苏中之间的一个主要摩擦来源：在1950年代的国际共产党会议上，中国人会攻击南斯拉夫“修正主义”，以此批评赫鲁晓夫；苏联人则会攻击中国的盟友、铁托的敌人阿尔巴尼亚，以此谴责中国的“教条主义”。这一切只是进一步侵蚀了国际共产主义。
en: Moreover, in the 1950s Khrushchev’s effort at a rapprochement with Tito brought the Soviet reform few advantages. True, in 1956 Tito gave his advance approval to Khrushchev’s crushing of the Hungarian secession as necessary for the defense of socialism, though he later criticized the severity of the repression. But he would never rejoin the “camp,” and instead became one of the founders, with Nehru, Nasser, and Sukarno, of the “nonaligned movement,” which was designed to be a third force in international affairs between NATO and the Soviet bloc. And although this force was more non-aligned in favor of the East than of the West, the Yugoslav regime because of its independence and its self-management socialism nonetheless set a bad example for the Soviets East European satellites. Finally, Yugoslavia remained a major source of friction between the Soviets and the Chinese: At international Communist gatherings in the fifties, the Chinese would attack Yugoslav “revisionism” as a way of criticizing Khrushchev, and the Soviets would attack China’s ally and Tito’s enemy, Albania, as a way of castigating Chinese “dogmatism.” All of this simply eroded international Communism still further.

zh: 但赫鲁晓夫与中国之间最重要的争点，也是他最重要的外交政策举措，是与西方、特别是与美国“和平共处”的政策。
这项新政策之所以出现，是因为斯大林之后需要通过提高民众生活水平来促进内部稳定，也因为对朝鲜冒险之后国际不稳定的真切恐惧。而这两种关切都与如何在核武器新时代进行“国际阶级斗争”的问题相联系。
en: But the most important bone of contention between Khrushchev and the Chinese, and his most important foreign policy initiative
, was the policy of “peaceful coexistence” with the West, and in particular with the United States.

This new policy arose because of the post-Stalin need to promote internal stability by improving the population’s living standard and because of genuine fear of international instability after the Korean misadventure. And both of these concerns were linked to the problem of how to wage the “international class war” in the new age of nuclear weapons.

zh: 因此，苏联人终于同意在朝鲜停战，并同意签订一项结束四国对奥地利占领的国家条约，还试探建立一个重新统一但保持中立的德国的可能性。这一缓和在1955年达到顶峰：赫鲁晓夫和布尔加宁在日内瓦与艾森豪威尔以及英国和法国总理举行会晤，这是战后苏联与西方领导人之间的首次峰会。尽管“日内瓦精神”当时被吹捧为标志着冷战的结束，但这次会晤实际上开启了两个超级大国之间漫长而动荡的关系，而这种关系很快将围绕它们在核军备上的竞争展开。
en: Accordingly, the Soviets at last agreed to an armistice in Korea as well as to a state treaty ending the four-power occupation of Austria, and they put out feelers for a reunited but neutralized Germany. This détente culminated in the first postwar summit between Soviet and Western leaders when Khrushchev and Bulganin met at Geneva in 1955 with Eisenhower and the prime ministers of Britain and France. Although the “spirit of Geneva” was touted at the time as marking the end of the Cold War, this meeting in fact inaugurated a long and stormy relationship between the two superpowers that would soon come to center around their rivalry in nuclear armaments.

zh: 但是，与美国缓和当然比苏联与铁托和解更让中国人反感，因为美国人在台湾海峡是中国的直接对手。因此，赫鲁晓夫在试图解决苏联与西方的问题时，进一步削弱了国际共产主义的凝聚力。他从前任那里继承来的铁板一块的遗产，就这样在外部迅速出现裂缝，其速度与它在内部受到的侵蚀一样快。苏联最高领导层中也不乏斯大林主义者，他们对赫鲁晓夫的创新感到惊恐，因而试图恢复旧秩序。这导致了赫鲁晓夫年代的第一次大危机：1957年6月，政治局多数同僚试图废黜他。
en: But détente with the United States was, of course, even more of an anathema to the Chinese than the Soviet rapprochement with Tito, for the Americans were the direct adversary of the Chinese in the Taiwan Straits. Therefore, in attempting to solve his problems with the West, Khrushchev was further undermining the cohesion of international Communism. The monolithic heritage he had received from his predecessor was thus being fissured externally as rapidly as it was eroding internally. Nor was there any lack of Stalinists in the Soviet high command to take alarm at Khrushchev’s innovations and so to attempt a restoration of the old order. And this led to the first great crisis of the Khrushchev years: In June 1957 a majority of his Politburo colleagues tried to depose him.

zh: 主要的不满来自秘密报告以及报告所引发的波兰和匈牙利的动荡。此外，讨好铁托、与中国日益紧张的关系以及与美国的缓和，都令老近卫感到担忧。而赫鲁晓夫即将推出的国内经济改革计划——稍后详述——也被认为同样危险。政治局对赫鲁晓夫的攻击由莫洛托夫、马林科夫和卡冈诺维奇领导。布尔加宁、伏罗希洛夫以及两位主要经济计划者马克西姆·萨布罗夫和米哈伊尔·佩尔武欣最终也加入了他们。但赫鲁晓夫拒绝向这一多数屈服并下台。他坚持认为，他只对选举他及其所有对手的中央委员会负责；他还成功地把会议拖延了足够多的天数，以便把他的支持者从各省召到莫斯科，而朱可夫元帅的空军为此提供了帮助。于是赫鲁晓夫获胜，他的批评者则被定为“反党集团”。但值得注意的是，该集团多数成员仍留在主席团，并将在那里再待几年。赫鲁晓夫还没有强大到能够把他们彻底清洗掉；而党此时也不会接受随意罢免显要领导人，因为如果赫鲁晓夫能这样做而不受惩罚，他接下来就能清洗任何其他人，就像他的前任曾经做到的那样。赫鲁晓夫正是在这种远非铁腕的党内机器控制下，开始了他重大的内部改革。
en: The main grievance was the secret speech and the Polish and Hungarian explosions the speech had provoked. Additionally, the wooing of Tito, the growing tension with the Chinese, and détente with the Americans were cause for concern to the old guard. And Khrushchev’s impending plans for internal economic reform—of which more shortly—were perceived as equally dangerous. The Politburo attack on Khrushchev was led by Molotov, Malenkov, and Kaganovich. They were eventually joined by Bulganin, Voroshilov, and two of the chief economic planners, Maksim Saburov and Mikhail Pervukhin. But Khrushchev refused to bow to this majority and step down. He insisted that he was responsible only to the Central Committee that had elected him and all his adversaries; and he succeeded in prolonging the meeting for a sufficient number of days to bring his supporters to Moscow from the provinces, an effort in which he was aided by Marshal Zhukov’s air force. Thus Khrushchev won, while his critics were condemned as “the Anti-Party Group.” But it is significant that most of the group remained members of the Presidium and would stay there for a few years more. Khrushchev was not strong enough to purge them outright; nor would the Party now accept the summary dismissal of prominent leaders, because if Khrushchev could get away with that, he could then purge anyone else, as his predecessor had been able to do. It is with this far less than iron control over the machinery of the Party that Khrushchev embarked on his great internal reforms.

zh: 赫鲁晓夫的“新政”
en: KHRUSHCHEV’S “NEW DEAL”

zh: 赫鲁晓夫的国内改革将全面扰乱旧的苏联秩序，因为他对斯大林本人的攻击，是去斯大林化和重塑整个苏联制度——农业、工业、国际关系以及党自身的运作——的努力的一部分。这并不是说赫鲁晓夫有一项宏伟的改革设计；他显然是在回应危机和对手的行动时才做了许多事情。但他也并不像人们常说的那样，一味临时拼凑，匆忙从一个大胆的纲领转向另一个。他的实验有一种模式和总方向。
尽管这一方向常被描述为“民粹主义”，赫鲁晓夫的民粹主义却是一种非常特殊的民粹主义，因为它只能与党一起、并通过党来实现。
en: Khrushchev’s domestic reforms would be upsetting to the old Soviet order all along the line, for his attack on Stalin the man was part of an effort to de-Stalinize and remold the whole Soviet system—agriculture, industry, international relations, and the functioning of the Party itself. This is not to say that Khrushchev had a grand design for reform; he clearly did much of what he did in response to crises and the actions of his opponents. But he was also not simply improvising his way from one bold program to another, as has often been alleged. There was a pattern and a general direction to his experiments.
Although this direction has often been described as “populist,” Khrushchev’s populism was of a very special kind, for it was to be realized only with and through the Party.

zh: 在赫鲁晓夫版本的列宁主义中，党和社会主义制度的使命是改善普通人民——党以其名义统治的工人和农民——的物质生活；正是在完成这一任务的过程中，社会主义才能显示出优于资本主义之处。斯大林不仅犯了罪，他还把党引离了正道，使人民陷入贫困。而赫鲁晓夫凭借对民众日常生活的广泛经验——无论是在莫斯科、乌克兰的集体农庄，还是在乌克兰前线的军队中——深知民众生活条件的恶劣。在这一点上，他与斯大林不同；正如我们所见，斯大林几乎从不离开克里姆林宫或附近的别墅。赫鲁晓夫当然清楚这种对比，并显然决心做一个不同类型的领袖。对赫鲁晓夫来说，社会主义意味着人民的物质丰裕；对他来说，最终提供这种丰裕应当是制度的首要任务。这意味着苏联传统的优先次序——重工业优先于轻工业、生产资料优先于消费品——必须颠倒过来。这又意味着减少军事生产，从而实行缓和与西方紧张关系的政策。赫鲁晓夫在他执政十一年的种种波折中，始终推行这套相互关联的措施。
en: In Khrushchev’s version of Leninism, the mission of the Party and of the socialist system was to improve the material existence of the simple people, the workers and peasants in whose name the Party ruled; it was in carrying out this task that socialism would show its superiority over capitalism. Stalin had not only committed crimes, he had diverted the Party from its true path and had plunged the people into poverty. And Khrushchev, through his extensive experience with the daily life of the population—whether in Moscow, on the kolkhozes of Ukraine, or in the army on the Ukrainian front—was well acquainted with the wretched conditions in which it lived. In this he was unlike Stalin who, as we have seen, almost never left the Kremlin or his nearby dacha. Khrushchev, of course, was well aware of this contrast and had clearly resolved to be a different type of leader. For Khrushchev, socialism meant material abundance for the people; for him, at last providing that abundance should be the system’s primary task. This meant that the traditional Soviet priority of heavy industry over light, and of producer over consumer goods, must be reversed. And this in turn entailed a decrease in military production, and hence a policy of reducing tensions with the West. It is this package of interrelated measures that Khrushchev consistently pursued through all the vicissitudes of his eleven years in power.

zh: 然而，最早在1953年公开提出这种优先次序颠倒的是马林科夫，而赫鲁晓夫当时反对他。其原因在于政治而非原则：马林科夫的倡议使军方和计划部门感到不安，于是赫鲁晓夫与他们结盟以除掉一个对手；随后，他多少像斯大林对待托洛茨基那样，采纳了对手的纲领。
en: It was Malenkov, however, who had first publicly proposed this reversal of priorities in 1953, and Khrushchev at that time had opposed him. The reason for this, however, was politics, not principle: The military and the planners were alarmed by Malenkov’s initiative, so Khrushchev allied with them to dispose of a rival; and then, somewhat as Stalin had done with Trotsky, he adopted his rival’s program.

zh: 但与斯大林不同，赫鲁晓夫从苏联经济最落后的领域——农业——开始。
对斯大林来说，集体农庄本质上是一种不付报酬便从农民那里榨取粮食供应的手段；赫鲁晓夫则力图把集体农庄改造成一个真正的经济机构，以不断提高生产率为导向。1953年，他发表了自集体化以来政府对农村状况的首次坦率评估，指出牲畜存栏数已降至1929年水平以下，甚至比革命前还少。随后他作出物质让步：降低自留地和家庭奶牛税，提高向国家义务交售农产品的收购价格，扩大拖拉机生产，并引入化肥。
en: But unlike Stalin, Khrushchev began with the most depressed area of the Soviet economy, agriculture.

For Stalin the kolkhoz had been essentially a means for extorting a food supply from the peasants without payment; Khrushchev aimed to transform the kolkhoz into a genuine economic institution oriented towards steadily rising productivity. In 1953 he gave the first frank governmental assessment since collectivization of conditions in the village, pointing out that the livestock population had fallen below its level of 1929 and was even smaller than it had been before the Revolution. He followed this with material concessions: Taxes were decreased on private plots and the family cow, prices for compulsory deliveries to the state were increased, the production of tractors was expanded, and chemical fertilizers were introduced.

zh: 但这一切都需要时间才能产生显著结果，而赫鲁晓夫希望迅速改善生活水平。于是1954年，他发动了一场老式布尔什维克攻势，在哈萨克斯坦北部和俄罗斯西伯利亚南部开垦约3500万公顷“生荒地”种植谷物。

在实地指挥这场运动的是赫鲁晓夫的长期门生勃列日涅夫，这项任务将成为后者调往莫斯科中央委员会之前的最后一块垫脚石。共青团积极分子被从城市派往半干旱的生荒草原组织国营农场；最终约有30万人定居在那里，到1956年，相当于加拿大全部耕地面积的广阔土地已投入生产。这场运动一度奏效：到那个十年结束时，苏联年度粮食收成平均有三分之一来自生荒地。但这一计划也极其浪费：干旱使生产充满风险，水土流失造成日益严重的损失。
en: But all of this would take time to produce significant results, and Khrushchev wanted a quick improvement in living standards. So in 1954 he launched an old-style Bolshevik offensive to open to grain cultivation some thirty-five million hectares of “virgin lands” in northern Kazakhstan and southern Russian Siberia.

It was Khrushchev’s longtime protégé, Brezhnev, who directed the campaign in the field, and this assignment would be the latter’s last stepping-stone before moving to the Central Committee in Moscow. Komsomol activists were dispatched from the cities to organize sovkhozes in the semiarid steppes of the virgin lands; some three hundred thousand people would eventually settle there, and by 1956 an expanse equivalent to the total cultivated area in Canada was in production. And the campaign worked for a time: on average, a third of the Soviet Union’s annual grain harvest came from the virgin lands by the end of the decade. But the program was also extremely wasteful: drought made production chancy, and soil erosion took an ever increasing toll.

zh: 生荒地的成功，使赫鲁晓夫农业战役的第二条战线成为可能。苏联的牲畜群以及由此而来的肉类产量很低，部分原因是缺乏饲料。来自西伯利亚的新粮食供应，使得可以把欧洲俄国更多的土地用于生产饲料，而赫鲁晓夫选择了单位面积产量高的玉米。1955年，通过法令在整个欧洲俄国推广玉米种植，但结果微不足道，因为这一地区大部分位置过于偏北，不宜种植这种作物。然而赫鲁晓夫仍强行推进。1957年，他发动了一场新运动，要在“肉、奶和黄油”产量上赶上美国，这无异于要在三到四年内使这些产品的产量提高两倍——一个不可能的目标。与此同时，他支持江湖骗子李森科，后者此时的影响力达到顶峰。
en: The success of the virgin lands made possible the second prong of Khrushchev’s agricultural campaign. Soviet livestock herds, and consequently meat production, were low, in part because of lack of fodder. The new grain supply from Siberia made it possible to devote more land in European Russia to producing fodder, and Khrushchev chose corn because of its high yield per acre. In 1955 corn production was introduced by decree throughout European Russia, though with only meager results, since most of this area was too far north for cultivating such a crop. Yet Khrushchev pressed on. In 1957 he launched a new campaign to catch up with the United States in the production of “meat, milk, and butter,” which meant nothing less than tripling the output of these products within three to four years—an impossible goal. At the same time, he lent support to the quack Lysenko, who now reached the height of his influence.

zh: 赫鲁晓夫农业实验的顶点，是1957—1958年对集体农庄制度的大规模重组。从精神上说，这项改革与他早先迷恋农业城以及马克思主义最终消灭“城乡对立”的目标相一致。为此，集体农庄受到合并压力，其总数从1950年的125,000个降至1958年的69,000个。与此同时，还发起了一场把集体农庄转变为国营农场的运动，国营农场的面积在这些年里翻了一番。这些变化当然与赫鲁晓夫早先关于农民家庭自留地的措施背道而驰；但它们非常符合布尔什维克传统精神，即把大型机械化集体作为农业的适当组织形式，因此也是赫鲁晓夫以党为中心的民粹主义的逻辑表达。事实上，在他统治末期，他还削减了家庭自留地的面积。
en: The culmination of Khrushchev’s agricultural experiments was a vast reorganization of the collective farming system in 1957-1958. In spirit this reform was consistent with his earlier infatuation with agrovilles and the Marxist goal of ultimately abolishing the “contradiction between town and country.”

this end kolkhozes were pressured to amalgamate, and their total number dropped from 125,000 in 1950 to 69,000 by 1958. At the same time, there was a drive to transform kolkhozes into sovkhozes, and the latter doubled their acreage during these years. These changes, of course, ran counter to Khrushchev’s earlier measures regarding the peasants’ family plots; but they were very much in the traditional Bolshevik spirit of large, mechanized collectives as the proper organization for agriculture, and were thus the logical expression of Khrushchev’s Party populism. In fact, towards the end of his reign he cut back the size of the family plots.

zh: 然而，赫鲁晓夫最后一项农业改革与以往所有政策背道而驰：1958年，此前作为党在农村控制基石的机器拖拉机站（MTS）被撤销，其机器卖给集体农庄。这一激进逆转的目的，是让扩大后的集体农庄和国营农场获得手段，成为理论上应有的现代社会主义生产单位。然而实际上，购买机器的费用和维护机器的问题成了集体农庄的新负担；机器拖拉机站的技术人员不愿被降为集体农庄庄员，因此许多人没有随机器迁移。因此，改革的结果令人失望：扩大后的集体农庄更容易被党控制，但它们使用机器的效率并不比旧制度下的集体农庄使用机器更高。
en: Khrushchev’s final agricultural reform, however, ran counter to all previous policy: in 1958 the Machine Tractor Stations (MTS), hitherto the cornerstone of Party control in the countryside, were abolished and their machines sold to the kolkhozes. The purpose of this radical reversal was to give the enlarged kolkhozes and sovkhozes the means to become the modern socialist units of production they were supposed to be in theory. In fact, however, the cost of purchasing the machines and the problem of maintaining them were a new burden on the kolkhozes; the skilled personnel of the MTS did not wish to be downgraded to the status of kolkhoz workers, so many of them did not relocate with their machines. The result of the reform, therefore, was disappointing: The enlarged kolkhozes were more easily controlled by the Party, but they could not use their machinery any more efficiently than their predecessors had used theirs under the old system.

zh: 那么，赫鲁晓夫在农村的努力效果如何？苏联农业的困境终于得到充分宣传，改善农业从此成为政权的一大关切。然而，这种关切的具体结果却不大。诚然，直到1958年，情况确有显著改善：农民收入上升，农民和城市居民都享受到更高的消费水平。但1958年以后，农业生产趋于平缓，随后下降。到1963年，在一场灾难性的歉收之后，苏联首次不得不从美国进口粮食，而关于玉米是赶上美国肉、奶、黄油产量之关键的谈论，已成为过去。那么，问题出在哪里？
en: So what was the effect of Khrushchev’s exertions in the countryside? The plight of Soviet agriculture was at last well publicized, and improving it would henceforth be a major concern of the regime. The concrete results of this concern, however, were modest. To be sure, up until 1958 matters did improve notably: Peasant incomes rose, and both the peasants and the city dwellers came to enjoy a higher standard of consumption. But after 1958 agricultural production levelled off and then declined, And by 1963, following a disastrous harvest, the Soviet Union for the first time had to import grain from the United States, while the talk of corn as the key to catching up with America in meat, milk, and butter was a thing of the past. So what went wrong?

zh: 首先，赫鲁晓夫的冲动和急躁妨碍了他的改革：一次重组紧接着另一次，速度快得让集体农庄陷入混乱状态。另一个问题是，赫鲁晓夫过于频繁地把一切押在单一解决方案上，无论是玉米、翻耕三叶草，还是开垦生荒地。他的积极主义还造成另一个问题：农民此时受到集体农庄管理层的更密切监督；特别是，与斯大林时期农村被忽视的那些年相比，他们更多地参与集体劳动，因此其自留地的产量相应下降。但赫鲁晓夫改革的主要缺陷在于，它们都是通过自上而下的法令推行的，并通过党的积极分子的突击战术实施：农民的主动性受到怀疑，人们期望集体农庄庄员服从命令，而不是回应激励。
en: First of all, Khrushchev’s impulsiveness and impatience hampered his reforms: one reorganization followed another so rapidly that the kolkhozes wound up in a state of disorganization. Another problem was that Khrushchev too often wagered everything on a single solution, whether it was corn, ploughing under clover, or opening virgin lands. His activism created yet another problem in that the peasants were now more closely supervised by the kolkhoz administration; in particular, they were more involved in collective labor than they had been during the years of Stalinist neglect, so the yield of their individual plots correspondingly declined. But the main defect of Khrushchev’s reforms was that they were all introduced by decree from above and implemented through the storm tactics of Party activists: peasant initiative was suspect, and the kolkhozniki were expected to respond to orders, not to incentives.

zh: 简而言之，赫鲁晓夫改良并扩大的集体农庄，只是共产主义惯常公式的又一表现：试图用政治手段解决经济问题。此外，他把集体农庄改造成经济机构的运动，只是进一步把农村政治化，因为这一努力完全来自党，而不是来自赫鲁晓夫无疑真诚地想要服务的人民。然而，增加民众主动性的价值此时已不言自明：家庭自留地的长期成功，以及战争期间“小组”制度的成就，都表明只有个人利益的激励才能改善农业生产。但这是非社会主义的，因此对赫鲁晓夫这位真诚的列宁主义者来说，也是倒退的、不可接受的。于是集体农庄继续作为神圣不可侵犯的苏联体制中的机构存在，莫斯科还为此建立了一个新的、更加浮夸的农业展览馆来彰显其荣耀。
en: In short, Khrushchev’s improved and enlarged collective farms were only another manifestation of the usual Communist formula of attempting to solve economic problems by political means. Moreover, his campaign to transform the kolkhoz into an economic institution simply politicized the countryside further, since this effort came entirely from the Party, not from the people that Khrushchev thought, no doubt sincerely, he was working for. And yet the value of increasing popular initiative was by now self-evident: the perennial success of the family plots, as well as the achievements of the link system during the war, showed that only the incentive of individual profit could improve agricultural production. But this was unsocialist, and thus for that true-believing Leninist, Khrushchev, it was also retrograde and unacceptable. So the kolkhoz continued as a sacrosanct Soviet institution, and a new and more boastful Agricultural Exhibition was erected to its glory in Moscow.

zh: 赫鲁晓夫在工业政策上同样精力充沛而激进。

然而在这里，由于工业与军队之间的密切联系，他不得不更加谨慎。毕竟，马林科夫正是因为优先发展消费品生产而非重工业，才被军方、计划人员和赫鲁晓夫本人的联盟推翻。而赫鲁晓夫个人也受惠于军方，尤其是朱可夫元帅，因为军方帮助除掉了贝利亚，更在1957年反党危机中挽救了局面。事实上，作为奖赏，朱可夫被任命为主席团候补委员，这是任何军事领袖首次获此殊荣。尽管如此，如果最终要满足民众的消费需求，赫鲁晓夫所谓的“食金属者”——重工业的老板们——就必须被赶下主导地位；而这当然意味着削减武装力量规模、减少装备开支。赫鲁晓夫通过用核武器和弹道武器（比常规军备便宜）安抚军方，解决了这个难题，这又使他能够把投资从重工业转向轻工业。与此同时，为了消除任何波拿巴主义的可能性，朱可夫元帅被解除政治局职务，并在访问阿尔巴尼亚期间被迫退休。
en: Khrushchev was similarly energetic and radical in his industrial policy.

Here, however, he had to tread with greater caution because of the intimate links between industry and the military. Malenkov had been overthrown, after all, by an alliance of the military, the planners, and Khrushchev himself, for giving preference to consumer production over heavy industry. And Khrushchev was personally beholden to the military, and in particular to Marshal Zhukov, for its aid in disposing of Beria and, even more, for saving the situation during the Anti-Party crisis of 1957. Indeed, as a reward Zhukov had been made an alternate member of the Presidium, the first time any military leader had been so honored. Nonetheless, the “metal-eaters,” as Khrushchev called the bosses of heavy industry, had to be dethroned from their predominance if the consumer needs of the population were at last to be met; and this, of course, meant reducing the size of the armed forces and spending less on their equipment. Khrushchev resolved this dilemma by appeasing the military with nuclear and ballistic weapons (which are less expensive than conventional armaments), and this in turn enabled him to shift investment from heavy to light industry. At the same time, to obviate any possibility of Bonapartism, Marshal Zhukov was removed from the Politburo and retired while on a visit to Albania.

zh: 但任何颠倒苏联工业优先次序的做法还有其他潜在反对者，那就是专业计划人员。自斯大林开始苏联工业建设以来的四分之一世纪里，国家工业设施及其计划机构的规模和复杂性都急剧增长。实际上，斯大林的制度一直是一种只设一个优先项目的战时经济：煤、铁、钢、机床和重型机械的综合体。整个事业于1930年由一个机构——最高国民经济委员会——启动。但到1932年，该机构已拆分为三个专业工业部；到三十年代末，已有二十个。战争和战后重建导致进一步的官僚膨胀，尤其是为军事需要，到1948年已有三十二个工业部。
en: But there were other potential opponents of any reversal of Soviet industrial priorities, and these were the professional planners. In the quarter century since Stalin had begun the Soviet industrial buildup, the national plant and its planning apparatus had grown enormously in size and in complexity. In effect, Stalin’s system had been a war economy with one priority: the complex of coal, iron, steel, machine tools, and heavy machinery. The whole enterprise had been launched in 1930 by one agency, Vesenkha. But by 1932 this agency had been broken into three specialized industrial ministries and by the end of the decade there were twenty. The war and the postwar reconstruction entailed further bureaucratic expansion, especially for military needs, to where by 1948 there were thirty-two industrial ministries.

zh: 这个利维坦在赫鲁晓夫治下继续增长，部分是为了跟上西方技术发展，例如电子技术，电视只是其中最显眼的例子；部分是为了给农业重新配备设备并满足其他消费需求，如服装和家庭用品。特别是，赫鲁晓夫发起了一项巨大的预制住房计划，以弥补斯大林时期最严重的匮乏之一，因为这种对民众的消费让步对制度的稳定已变得必不可少。而这种优先事项的增多，又造就了更多工业部和其他经济部，到1950年代末已约有四十个；这种增长使资源分配、协调和计划的任务更加复杂。尽管如此，计划机构及其此时庞大的专业人员队伍，仍然忠于重冶金这一旧有的压倒性优先项目。
en: This Leviathan continued to grow under Khrushchev, in part to keep up with Western technological developments, as in electronics, of which television was only the most visible example, and in part to reequip agriculture and meet other consumer needs, such as clothing and household goods. In particular, Khrushchev launched a huge program of prefabricated housing to make up for one of the worst lacks of the Stalin years, for such consumer concessions to the population had become imperative for the system’s stability. And this multiplication of priorities created more industrial and other economic ministries, to where by the late 1950s they numbered around forty, a growth which created a more complicated task of resource allocation, coordination, and planning. Nonetheless, the planning apparatus, with its now huge corps of professionals, remained devoted to the old overriding priority of heavy metallurgy.

zh: 因此，1957年，赫鲁晓夫决定通过废除大部分中央部委、把其职能分散到约150个地区经济委员会（即国民经济委员会）来松动制度。只有军备、化工和电力仍归中央控制。这种对部委帝国的拆解，触怒了中央和制度上层根深蒂固的干部名录体系中的既得利益，但它在地区党的队伍中找到了支持，而赫鲁晓夫的基本支持力量历来就在那里。这项改革也造成大量行政混乱，因为中央计划仍然存在，而协调地方委员会活动的手段此时却不足。
en: In 1957, therefore, Khrushchev decided to limber up the system by abolishing most of the central ministries and dispersing their functions to some 150 regional economic councils, or sovnarkhozes. Only armaments, chemicals, and electricity were to remain under central control. This breakup of ministerial empires alienated entrenched

interests at the center and in the higher echelons of the system, but it found support in the regional Party ranks where Khrushchev had always had his basic clientele. This reform also generated much administrative confusion, for the central Plan remained, yet the means for coordinating the activities of the local councils were now deficient.

zh: 尽管如此，赫鲁晓夫仍继续推进他的创新，因为他本人和制度此时都确实春风得意。1957年，苏联以第一颗人造卫星震惊世界，这一壮举不仅宣传了其技术的进步，也展示了其在弹道导弹方面的实力。苏联的太空成就继续不断：1959年无人探测器抵达月球，1961年尤里·加加林成为第一个进入太空的人。这些成就只会加强赫鲁晓夫对苏联制度内在优越性的信念，而这种优越性甚至开始在西方许多人眼中显得确有可能。
en: Still, Khrushchev pressed on with his innovations, for he, and the system, were now riding very high indeed. In 1957 the Soviet Union astonished the world with the first Sputnik, a feat that not only advertised the progress of her technology but also demonstrated her prowess in ballistic missiles. And Soviet space exploits continued, with an unmanned landing on the moon in 1959 and the first man in space, Iurii Gagarin, in 1961. Khrushchev’s belief in the intrinsic superiority of the Soviet system was only reinforced by these achievements, and that superiority even began to appear as a real possibility to many in the West.
