zh: 他的个人权力也在增长。

1958年，他解除曾站在反党集团一边的布尔加宁的总理职务，自己兼任该职，从而像斯大林一样，把党的首脑和政府首脑的角色集于一身。他还废除了当时的第六个五年计划，代之以宏大的七年计划。为了批准这一背离苏联常规的做法，1959年他采取了同样激进的措施，提前两年召开第二十一次党代表大会，这是苏联历史上第一次这样的“非常”代表大会。同年，在一系列出访——印度、中国、南斯拉夫和西欧——之后，他又访问美国，并在戴维营与艾森豪威尔举行另一次峰会。这种不知疲倦的环球旅行与其前任深居简出的习惯形成对比，激发了世界的想象，似乎证明了苏联对和平共处承诺的真诚。“戴维营精神”从“日内瓦精神”手中接过火炬，冷战看上去正在逐渐平息。
en: His personal power also increased.

In 1958 he removed Bulganin, who had sided with the Anti-Party Group, as prime minister and assumed that post himself, thus combining, as had Stalin, the roles of Party chief and government head. He also scrapped the then current Sixth Five-Year Plan and replaced it with a grandiose Seven-Year Plan. To approve this departure from Soviet practice, in 1959 he resorted to the equally radical measure of convening a Party Congress, the Twenty-first, two years early, the first such “extraordinary” Congress in Soviet history. And in the same year, he capped a series of forays abroad—which had taken him to India, China, Yugoslavia, and Western Europe—by a visit to the United States and another summit meeting with Eisenhower at Camp David. The contrast between this tireless world travelling and the reclusive habits of his predecessor sparked the world’s imagination and seemed to demonstrate the sincerity of the Soviet Union’s commitment to peaceful coexistence. The “spirit of Camp David” took up the torch from the “spirit of Geneva,” and the Cold War appeared to be winding down.

zh: 但1957—1960年最终成为赫鲁晓夫自上而下小型革命的顶点。此后，他设法从制度中榨取的绩效的增幅开始下降。他遭遇了一系列国际挫折。而他不知疲倦地推进内部重组，在党内引起了广泛反对。
en: But the years 1957-1960 turned out to be the climax of Khrushchev’s minirevolution from above. Thereafter, the increase in performance he had managed to squeeze out of the system began to decline. He met a series of international reverses. And his tireless campaigns of internal reorganization generated widespread opposition within the Party.

zh: 1960年代初，赫鲁晓夫农业计划的失败，又因工业重组的瓦解而雪上加霜。事实证明，国民经济委员会无论是在其指定区域内运作，还是在与其他区域协调活动时，都无法有效运转，必须不断请示中央。一个地区的拖拉机厂需要另一个地区工厂生产的钢材和设备，而两个地区都需要中央提供信贷和物资。全联盟国家计划委员会继续从事长期规划，而各加盟共和国的计划委员会则负责执行全联盟计划。为了确保这些层级之间以及各地区之间的协调，一种悄然进行的再集中化很快以专门国家委员会的形式出现，其职能与旧部委大致相同，人员也相同。1963年，一次大合并把国民经济委员会的数量减少了一半，并把它们全部置于一个超级协调机构之下，该机构沿用了旧的布尔什维克名称“最高国民经济委员会”。于是，赫鲁晓夫的工业改革实际上被撤销了。与此同时，生产陷入混乱，苏联的经济增长率开始下降，这种下降将持续到1991年的崩溃。
en: At the beginning of the sixties the failure of Khrushchev’s agricultural program was compounded by the disintegration of his industrial reorganization. It turned out that the sovnarkhozes could not operate effectively, either within their own designated regions or in coordinating activity with other regions, without constant reference to the center. A tractor factory in one region needed steel and equipment produced by factories in another, and both regions required credits and supplies from the center. A national Gosplan continued to conduct prospective planning, while republican Gosplans were charged with implementation of the all-Union plans. In order to insure coordination between these levels and among the regions, a creeping recentralization soon emerged in the form of special state committees with approximately the same functions as the old ministries and the same personnel. In 1963 a great merger of sovnarkhozes reduced their number by half, and all of them were placed under a supercoordinating agency with the old Bolshevik name Supreme Economic Council. Thus Khrushchev’s industrial reform was virtually undone. In the meantime, production had been disorganized and the Soviet rate of economic growth began a decline that would continue until the collapse of 1991.

zh: 国民经济委员会失败，并不是因为赫鲁晓夫以他一贯的冲动方式草率拼凑了它们——尽管这确实是问题的一部分——而是因为它们违背了制度的本性。在没有市场来分配资源的情况下，这项任务不可避免地成为指令性计划的职能；也就是说，生产决策是按照政治而非经济标准以行政方式作出的。但指令性计划必须能够指挥，否则一切都会在混乱中崩溃。换句话说，指令性计划必须集中化才能运转，把它的活动划分为不同区域或层级，会破坏必要的分配指挥链。这就像在战役进行中授予军队各师决策自主权；而正如我们所见，苏联式指令性计划本质上是一种制度化的战时经济。因此，苏联制度为了自卫，自发地重新集中化，以对抗赫鲁晓夫的国民经济委员会。
en: The sovnarkhozes failed not because Khrushchev had concocted them in his usual impetuous way—although this was indeed a part of the problem—but because they went against the grain of the system. In the absence of a market to allocate resources, this task inevitably becomes the function of a directive plan; that is, one where production decisions are made administratively according to political, not economic, criteria. But a directive plan has to direct, otherwise everything collapses in confusion. In other words, directive planning must be centralized to function at all, and dividing up its activities into zones or layers destroys the necessary chain of allocative command. It is like granting decisional autonomy to the divisions of an army in the midst of a campaign; and the Soviet-style directive plan, as we have seen, is in essence an institutionalized war economy. The Soviet system, therefore, spontaneously recentralized itself in self-defense against Khrushchev’s sovnarkhozes.

zh: 然而，这并不意味着他没有在解决命令经济固有的实际缺陷。第一个缺陷源于这样一个事实：在任何生产过程中，需要作出的决策数量都太多，无法预先计算或由中央指导。因此，任何这样的计划本质上都严重不完整，必须靠来自基层的不断反馈加以纠正。在正常的或市场的经济中，这些输入由真实价格提供，而不是由苏联式制度的政治价格提供。在没有这种真实价格的情况下，分权便成为纠正计划僵化的主要手段。但分权同样只是一种行政或政治手段，而不是经济手段。因此，它只是延续了它本应纠正的问题，或仅仅把问题转移到另一个层级。斯大林之后几十年间的大多数苏联经济改革，本质上都是这类表面的解决办法。
en: This does not mean, however, that he was not attacking real deficiencies inherent in a command economy. The first of these stems from the fact that in any productive process the number of decisions to be made is too large for advance calculation or central direction. Any such plan, therefore, is by its very nature woefully incomplete, and it must consequently be corrected by constant inputs from below. In a normal, or market, economy these inputs are furnished by real prices, not by the political prices of a Soviet-type system. Failing such real prices, decentralization becomes the principal means for correcting the rigidity of the plan. But decentralization, too, is only an administrative or political, not an economic, device. It thus only continues, or simply transposes to another level, the problem it was supposed to correct. And most Soviet economic reforms over the post-Stalin decades were essentially pseudosolutions of this sort.

zh: 指令性计划的另一个缺陷是内生的停滞倾向。计划需要中央的垄断性部委，而这些部委往往会变成自我延续的王国。此外，计划由过去经验的外推构成，这些经验被量化为统计数据，然后再循环为“控制数字”，作为未来生产的目标。因此，计划每年往往生产出与以前相同的东西，只是数量有所增加，重点也相应地放在数量而非质量上。在这样的世界里，新产品或新设计具有破坏性，因为它们的引入会拖慢计划完成率的增长，还会使有关人员损失奖金。
en: Another deficiency of directive planning is an inbuilt tendency to stagnation. The Plan requires central, monopolistic ministries, and these tend to become self-perpetuating empires. The Plan, moreover, is made up of projections from past experience, as quantified in statistics, which are then recycled into “control figures” which serve as targets for future production. Thus each year the Plan tends to produce what it did before, only multiplied somewhat, and the emphasis is correspondingly on quantity, not quality. In such a world new products or designs are disruptive because their introduction causes delays in the upward march of Plan percentages as well as losses of rewards.

zh: 由于这种例行公事的精神，为重冶金设计的原始斯大林主义计划机制几乎从未产生技术创新或开发新产品。而当战后年代从西方引入这类创新和产品时，计划体系越来越难以适应；随着工业前沿从化工和塑料推进到电子，再到计算机，这一点变得十分明显。每引入一种新产品或新技术，就会建立一个新部，发动一场突击“运动”，几年后制度或多或少会赶上西方——但到那时，技术进步的前沿又已向前推进。只有在军备领域，尤其是核武器和弹道武器领域，苏联经济的政治方法才真正有效并具有国际竞争力。至于其他方面，离军事部门越远，经济表现就越差。
en: As a result of this spirit of routine, the primitive Stalinist planning mechanisms designed for heavy metallurgy almost never produced technological innovations or developed new products. And when, in the postwar years, such innovations and products were introduced from the West, the planning system had increasing difficulty in adapting; this became painfully evident as the industrial cutting-edge advanced from chemicals and plastics to electronics, and then to computers. Each time a new product or technology was introduced, a new ministry would be created, a crash “campaign” would be launched, and in a few years the system would more or less catch up with the West—but by then the frontier of technological progress would have moved forward once again. Only in the area of armaments, especially nuclear and ballistic, were the political methods of the Soviet economy genuinely effective and internationally competitive. For the rest, the farther one got from the military sector, the worse the economic performance became.

zh: 因此，赫鲁晓夫晚年的危机是“系统性的”。它源于计划体制的僵化和内在保守主义，再加上二战后对该制度不断扩大的要求。因此，苏联一度令人瞩目的增长率在1958年以后持续下降，尽管苏联仍被普遍认为是“世界第二大经济体”，这一地位却越来越受到质疑。于是赫鲁晓夫继续推进新的政治纲领，以解决他的经济问题。
en: The crisis of the late Khrushchev years was thus “systemic.” It was due to the institutional rigidity and the inherent conservatism of the planning system, in conjunction with the constantly expanding demands made on that system after the Second World War. Accordingly, the once impressive Soviet rate of growth declined steadily after 1958, and although the Soviet Union was still generally considered to be the “world’s second-largest economy,” this status was increasingly called into doubt. So Khrushchev plowed on with new political programs for solving his economic problems.

zh: 自生荒地计划以来，赫鲁晓夫改革努力的主旨一直是把经济考虑置于政治考虑之前，并优先考虑消费者利益，而非“食金属者”为增长而增长的做法。
这些态度共同构成了赫鲁晓夫版本的新经济政策——当然，这是一种没有市场的新经济政策，而且是在斯大林之后的背景下，但无论如何是一种具有修正主义精神的新经济政策。而“修正主义”正是他在北京的对手，以及在莫斯科私下议论的对手，给赫鲁晓夫政策扣上的恶名。因为这项政策不仅颠倒了公认的斯大林主义优先次序；它还挑战了此时已庞大而根深蒂固的管理和计划官僚集团的习惯与信念。
en: Ever since the virgin lands program, the thrust of Khrushchev’s reform efforts had been to put economic considerations ahead of political ones, and to favor consumer interests over the “metal-eaters’” pursuit of growth for growth’s sake.

These attitudes together constitute Khrushchev’s version of the NEP—to be sure, a NEP without a market and in a post-Stalin context, but a NEP in revisionist spirit nonetheless. And “revisionism” was the opprobrious epithet applied to Khrushchev’s policies by his adversaries in Peking and,

, in Moscow. For this policy was not only a reversal of accepted Stalinist priorites; it was also a challenge to the habits and convictions of the by now enormous and well-entrenched managerial and planning bureaucracies.

zh: 因此，到1961年，赫鲁晓夫在农业和工业方面的改革都遭到党内机关越来越强烈的抵制。事实上，这种抵制根源于1957年6月的反党集团事件。导致那场未遂政变的因素之一，是赫鲁晓夫两个月前提出建立地区国民经济委员会；但在该集团眼中，最后的挑衅是赫鲁晓夫要在可笑的四年时间内“在肉、奶和黄油上赶上美国”的运动。稍后，他又发动运动推广种植玉米作饲料，并翻耕斯大林曾偏爱的三叶草，这令党务官僚们恼火。但正统派的敌意达到顶点，是因为废除机器拖拉机站——它在社会主义农业中的地位，犹如冶金在社会主义工业中的地位——以及转向七年计划。这种敌意更加危险，因为尽管赫鲁晓夫击败了该集团，却没有粉碎它，因为他未能把其成员开除出党。因此，在他看来，改革的主要障碍是党仍然带有斯大林主义色彩。于是，在1961年秋按计划召开的第二十二次党代表大会上，他试图通过一场党内政治革命和发动第二次去斯大林化运动，来推进他的经济纲领。
en: By 1961, therefore, Khrushchev’s reforms in both agriculture and industry were encountering increasing resistance from the Party apparat. Indeed, this resistance had its roots in the affair of the Anti-Party Group of June 1957. One of the factors leading to that abortive coup had been Khrushchev’s move two months earlier to introduce sovnarkhozes, but the final provocation in the eyes of the Group had been Khrushchev’s campaign to “overtake the United States in meat, milk, and butter” in the ridiculous span of four years. Somewhat later, the apparatchiki were riled by his campaigns to generalize the growing of corn for fodder and to plow under the clover once favored by Stalin. But the hostility of the orthodox was brought to a peak by the abolition of the MTS—as much a fetish in socialist agriculture as metallurgy was in socialist industry—together with the switch to a Seven-Year Plan. This hostility was all the more threatening because, although Khrushchev had defeated the Group, he had not crushed it, for he had been unable to expel its members from the Party. In his view, therefore, the main impediment to reform was the still Stalinist cast of the Party. So at the regularly scheduled Twenty-second Party Congress in the fall of 1961 he sought to advance his economic programs by a political revolution in the Party and by launching a second de-Stalinization campaign.

zh: 这次代表大会最初的目的，是批准新的党纲，这是自1903年以来的第三部、也是自1919年以来的第一部党纲。由于前两份文件都是列宁的著作，这次代表大会对党来说标志着一个具有象征意义的重要时刻，赫鲁晓夫决心充分利用它。他的纲领旨在引导国家走向“无产阶级专政”的终结，从而实现“向共产主义的过渡”。赫鲁晓夫起初想要一份未来的详细蓝图，甚至明确规定“国家的消亡”以及由党——最终是“全体人民的党”——作为社会自我管理的唯一机构来取代国家。但他被同僚迫使放弃这些乌托邦目标，这只会使他对他认为是同僚从中阻挠的行为越发不耐烦。
en: The initial purpose of the Congress was to approve a new Party Program, only the third since 1903 and the first since 1919. Because the two previous documents had been the work of Lenin, the Congress marked a symbolically important moment for the Party, and Khrushchev resolved to make the most of it. His program was intended to guide the country to the end of the “dictatorship of the proletariat” and thus to effect the “transition to communism.” Khrushchev initially wanted a detailed blueprint for the future, even spelling out the “withering away of the state” and its replacement by the Party—at last the “Party of all the people”—as the sole institution of society’s self-management. But he was compelled by his colleagues to drop these utopian goals, and this only increased his impatience with what he considered their obstructionism.

zh: 即便如此，代表大会的口号仍宣称“这一代苏联人将生活在共产主义社会”，而新党纲轻率地承诺，这一豪言将在1980年“基本”实现。党纲还包括未来二十年每年10%增长率的预测，并在此基础上预言苏联将在1970年超过美国——美国的年增长率仅为2.5%。在西方，《纽约时报》和《世界报》等重量级报纸认真对待这些说法，尽管未必完全照字面理解。事实上，赫鲁晓夫心中的设想比这些数字所暗示的要温和一些。共产主义社会“各尽所能，按需分配”并不是某座幻想中的水晶城；用平淡的话说，它意味着住房以及交通、公用事业等服务将免费。这是一种为普通人提供充分社会保障和平等主义的乌托邦；但它也意味着一种静止的需求水平，一旦现代工业基础“建成”，就不再需要经济继续扩张。因为赫鲁晓夫相信苏联制度本质上已经获得了这一基础，所以他可以非常真诚地宣称，完整共产主义即将到来，他的国家已经配得上“天堂”之名。而这种关于“光辉未来”在具体意义上意味着什么的朴素期待，在他较为单纯的同胞中非常普遍。
en: Even so, the slogan of the Congress proclaimed that “the present generation of Soviet people will live under Communism,” and the new Party Program rashly promised that this boast would be realized, “in the main,” by 1980. The Program also included projections of a 10 percent annual growth rate over the next two decades, and on this basis it predicted that the Soviet Union would overtake the United States—whose per annum rate of growth was a mere 2.5 percent—by 1970. And in the West, such heavyweight newspapers as the
and

took these claims seriously, if not exactly literally. In fact, Khrushchev had in mind something more modest than these figures seemed to suggest. The communist society of “from each according to his abilities, to each according to his needs” was not some visionary crystalline city; prosaically, it meant that housing and such services as transportation and utilities would be free. It was a utopia of full social security and egalitarianism for the common man; but it also implied a static level of needs that did not require an expanding economy once the modern industrial base had been “built.” Because Khrushchev believed the Soviet system had essentially acquired this base, he could quite sincerely claim that full communism was nigh and that his country already deserved to be called “paradise.” And this naive expectation of what the “radiant future” would mean in concrete terms was very widespread among his simpler compatriots.

zh: 但根深蒂固的机关正在阻挡通往这一未来的道路，因此代表大会的实际事务是设计打破干部抵制的手段。于是，赫鲁晓夫推动修改党章，规定中央委员会或主席团成员最多任三届五年；在地区和地方一级，新规则把官员限制为三届两年。尽管对特别合格的领导人允许例外，但如果这些新规则付诸实施，将终结所有党务官僚自斯大林死后享有的实际终身任期。受威胁最大的党的人员，是此前构成赫鲁晓夫主要支持基础的中层省级领导人；尽管他们遵照第一书记的要求投票支持新章程，但他们的反应实际上是敌对的。这一结果凸显了制度的另一个结构性困境：任期限制是使机关对除党务官僚之外的任何人负责的唯一办法，但与此同时，它又必然在机关及其最高领袖之间造成冲突，而最高领袖的任期却不受限制。
en: But the entrenched apparat was barring the way to this future, and so the practical business of the Congress was to devise means to break the cadres’ resistance. Accordingly, Khrushchev pushed through a revision of Party statutes limiting members of the Central Committee or its Presidium to three five-year terms; at the regional and local levels, the new rule limited officials to three two-year terms. Although exceptions were allowed for unusually qualified leaders, these new rules, if applied, would have ended the virtual life tenure that all apparatchiki had enjoyed since Stalin’s death. The Party figures most threatened were the middle-level provincial leaders who had hitherto been Khrushchev’s main base of support; although they dutifully voted for the new statutes, as the First Secretary demanded, their reaction was in fact hostile. And this outcome highlighted another structural dilemma of the system: A term limit was the only way to make the apparat accountable to anyone but the apparatchiki themselves, yet at the same time it set up an inevitable conflict between the apparat and its supreme leader, whose term, moreover, was not limited.

zh: 1962年秋，赫鲁晓夫把党的等级体系一分为二，一半负责农业，一半负责工业，从而使这种冲突的可能性进一步加剧。这一变革的理由，是让党的官员督促工厂和集体农庄提高生产率，同时让这些官员对失败直接负责。于是，每个省和区此时都有两套官员等级体系，而两套体系的管辖范围重叠、职能相互冲突，因为任何特定地区的工业和农业运作都无法整齐分开。此外，党的干部几十年来主要关心政治和意识形态工作。他们在经济生产中的角色是总监督者、危机中的排障者以及政权警察；他们一直是制度在企业中的耳目，也是企业在制度中的代言人。然而此时，他们被要求在生产中扮演直接角色，而他们既不具备相应能力，又对此感到反感。在他们看来，党被颠倒了，政治被不恰当地置于经济之下。而事实上，这项改革确实导致制度运作进一步混乱，生产进一步下降。
en: In the fall of 1962 Khrushchev compounded this potential for conflict by splitting the Party hierarchy in two, making one half responsible for agriculture and the other half for industry. The rationale for this change was to make Party officials ride herd on factories and kolkhozes to increase productivity, and at the same time make these officials directly responsible for failures. Thus every province and district now had two hierarchies of officials, and each hierarchy had overlapping jurisdictions and clashing functions, since industrial and agricultural operations in any given area could not be neatly separated. Party functionaries, moreover, had for decades been concerned primarily with political and ideological work. Their role in economic production had been that of general supervisor, troubleshooter in a crisis, and regime policeman; they had been the eyes and the ears of the system in the enterprises, and the advocates of the enterprises to the system. Now, however, they were being asked to assume a direct role in production, one for which they were not qualified and which they resented. In their view, the Party had been stood on its head, and politics had been improperly subordinated to economics. And in truth the reform did result in a further confusion in the operation of the system and a further decline in production.

zh: 于是，制度的这个结构性困境再次被凸显出来。为了解决一个经济问题，赫鲁晓夫诉诸政治解决方案，因为在苏联条件下，经济与政治不可分割地交织在一起。然而，事实上他只是制造了又一个自我挫败的伪改革，因为经济力量无法通过纯粹的行政重组来解放；只有使它们彻底摆脱政治控制才有可能。但这不可能，因为那将剥夺党存在的理由，而赫鲁晓夫和机关都不准备考虑这一点。
en: So the structural dilemma of the system had once again been highlighted. In order to solve an economic problem Khrushchev had resorted to a political solution, for under Soviet conditions the economic and the political were inextricably intertwined. Yet, in fact, he had only produced another self-defeating pseudoreform, for economic forces could not be liberated by a purely administrative restructuring; they could be liberated only if they were freed from political control
. But this was impossible because it would deprive the Party of its raison d’être, and this neither Khrushchev nor the apparat were prepared to contemplate.

zh: 赫鲁晓夫对党的结构的改组，伴随着第二次去斯大林化运动；这场运动始于第二十二次党代表大会，贯穿整个1962年。二十大上对斯大林的攻击，对国际共产主义运动和整个外部世界影响最大。而这场新运动将在苏联国内产生最深刻的影响，不可逆转地改变文化氛围。
en: Khrushchev’s shake-up of Party structures was accompanied by a second de-Stalinization campaign, which began at the Twenty-second Party Congress and unfolded throughout 1962. The attack on Stalin at the Twentieth Congress had had its greatest impact on the international Communist movement and on the outside world in general. The new campaign would have its most profound impact within the Soviet Union, where it changed the cultural atmosphere irrevocably.

zh: 在二十二大上，赫鲁晓夫没有按照预先准备的议程行事，再次猛烈攻击斯大林的罪行。但这一次，他是在公开场合、通过国家电台进行攻击，并得到一连串志同道合演说者的附和。代表大会随后表决把斯大林的遗体从列宁墓中移出；遗体被埋在克里姆林宫墙边，上面压着一层混凝土。斯大林雕像在全苏联被推倒，他的名字从机构和城市中消失，甚至包括神圣的斯大林格勒，该城被平淡地改名为伏尔加格勒。
en: At the Twenty-second Congress, Khrushchev departed from the prepared scenario and again launched into a vehement attack on Stalin’s crimes. But this time he made the attack in public and over national radio, and he was seconded by a succession of like-minded orators. The Congress then voted to remove Stalin’s body from the Lenin Mausoleum; it was buried beside the Kremlin wall under a load of concrete. Stalin’s statues came down across the Soviet Union and his name disappeared from institutions and cities, including even the sacred site of Stalingrad, which became tritely Volgograd.

zh: 这一切令全国震惊，却没有改变党的习惯，于是次年赫鲁晓夫又争取自由派知识分子的帮助，发动了一场更大胆的运动。《真理报》发表了叶夫根尼·叶夫图申科的诗《斯大林的后继者》，矛头指向机关中所有仍然在世的小暴君，并呼吁保持警惕，守住克里姆林宫墙边那块新的“墓碑石板”。在苏联生活中初生的隐蔽政治里，这是一项重大宣言。
en: All this astounded the country but did not change the habits of the Party, so the next year Khrushchev enlisted the help of the liberal intelligentsia for an even bolder campaign.

published a poem of Yevgenii Yevtushenko, “The Heirs of Stalin,” aimed at all the still-living lesser despots of the apparat and calling for a vigilant guard over the new “gravestone slab” beside the Kremlin wall. In the nascent shadow politics of Soviet life, this was a major declaration.

zh: 然而更重要的是，1962年11月，《新世界》发表了近年获释但仍默默无闻的泽克亚历山大·索尔仁尼琴的中篇小说《伊凡·杰尼索维奇的一天》，这是对古拉格生活的首次描绘。

人们立即得知，“他本人”批准了这部作品，而且这被视为一个信号：“不仅是一场运动，而且是一项政策”。事实上，赫鲁晓夫得到的远比他预想的多。他的目标是有限的：震动党，让制度与自己的过去和解，从而净化制度。而索尔仁尼琴的知识分子支持者们的目标则更宏大：把文化从党的控制下解放出来，彻底摧毁斯大林主义的“谎言”。自1953年解冻以来，尤其是在《日瓦戈医生》事件之后，苏联作家在纸上描写斯大林时代时越来越大胆。问题是如何把它付印。于是《新世界》主编亚历山大·特瓦尔多夫斯基抓住第二次去斯大林化运动的时机，选中索尔仁尼琴的中篇小说，作为最有可能实现突破的载体；他设法把小说送到赫鲁晓夫私人秘书手中，后者在零碎的时间里读给领袖听。小说民粹主义的语调（主人公是个普通工人）打动了赫鲁晓夫，他热情地把它分发给主席团批准。有了这份批文在手，特瓦尔多夫斯基便放手行事，结果这成了赫鲁晓夫时代的第二颗重磅炸弹。
en: Far more important, however, in November 1962
published the novella of a recently returned but still unknown
, Aleksandr Solzhenitsyn’s

children: One Day in the Life of Ivan Denisovich

en: , the first depiction of life in the Gulag.

It immediately became known that “He Himself” had authorized it, and that it was intended to be the signal “not just for a campaign, but for a policy.” In fact, Khrushchev got a great deal more than he had bargained for. His aim was the limited one of shaking up the Party and purging the system by having it come to terms with its past. The aim of Solzhenitsyn’s intelligentsia sponsors was the vaster one of liberating culture from Party control and definitively demolishing the Stalinist Lie. Ever since the thaw of 1953, and especially after the coup of
, Soviet writers had been growing bolder in what they put on paper about the Stalin era. The problem was to get it into print. So

’s editor, Aleksandr Tvardovskii, seizing the occasion of the second de-Stalinization drive, selected Solzhenitsyn’s novella as the most likely vehicle for a breakthrough; he managed to transmit it to Khrushchev’s personal secretary, who read it to the leader at odd moments. Its populistic tone (the hero was a simple worker) struck a responsive chord, and Khrushchev enthusiastically distributed it to the Presidium for approval. With this imprimatur in his pocket, Tvardovskii went ahead with what turned out to be the second great bombshell of the Khrushchev era.

zh: 因为这篇小说超越了攻击斯大林，隐含地攻击了制度本身。劳改营第一次在苏联被公开提及，因此它们的存在——西方许多人仍否认这一点——得到了政权本身的确认。更重要的是，秘密报告只谈斯大林对党的罪行，而《伊凡·杰尼索维奇》把焦点转向人民的苦难；这使民众得出结论：去斯大林化此时应当成为解放社会的普遍进程。一整套去斯大林化的文学开始出现。安娜·阿赫玛托娃第一次敢于写下她关于1937年的诗作《安魂曲》，安德烈·阿马尔里克等年轻作家也开始创作。诚然，这些作品大多未能付印。但正如阿赫玛托娃所说，它们以“前古腾堡”的方式，作为萨米兹达特流传开来；而且常常在西方“那边”作为塔米兹达特出版，再由电台读回俄国。
en: For the story went beyond an attack on Stalin to an implicit attack on the system as such. The camps were for the first time mentioned publicly in the Soviet Union, and thus their existence—which many people in the West still denied—was certified by the regime itself. Even more, whereas the secret speech had addressed only Stalin’s crimes against the Party,

shifted the focus to the sufferings of the people; and this led the population to conclude that de-Stalinization should now become a general process of liberating society. A whole literature of de-Stalinization began to emerge. Anna Akhmatova for the first time dared to write down her poem on. 1937, “Requiem,” and younger writers, such as Andrei Amalrik, began to produce. To be sure, most of this output did not get into print. But in “pre-Gutenberg” fashion, as Akhmatova said, it did get distributed as
; and quite often it was published “over there” in the West as
, and then read back to Russia by radio.

zh: 因此，到赫鲁晓夫统治末期，一种异见文化诞生了。自1920年代以来，俄国第一次出现了批判性的公众舆论和雏形的公民社会。此时，这个新批判知识分子群体的成员还没有想过反对政权，更不用说设法终结它。他们都严格处在改革共产主义的限度内，即使像索尔仁尼琴这样愤懑的人也不例外。他们所要求的只是关于过去的“真相”。然而，这种平淡的、经验性的真相一旦追究到底，就不可避免地会摧毁那个作为整体制度的“谎言”。正统的守护者，例如中央委员会负责意识形态的书记米哈伊尔·苏斯洛夫，立即明白了这一点，并着手煽动反击。《伊凡·杰尼索维奇》发表一个月后，赫鲁晓夫被诱去参观一个抽象画展，结果他大发雷霆，连声咒骂，并说“驴子用尾巴都画得比这好”。于是倒退开始了：索尔仁尼琴在俄国只又发表了两篇小说，古拉格不再是文学题材。尽管如此，对制度可信性的损害，正如二十大后对“崇拜”的损害一样，已无法挽回。随着二十二大后的伟大解冻，以及他对党的重组，赫鲁晓夫在试图改革共产主义时，无意中开启了颠覆共产主义的漫长进程。
en: So by the end of Khrushchev’s reign a culture of dissidence was born. For the first time since the 1920s critical public opinion and an embryonic civil society existed in Russia. For the moment, the members of this new critical intelligentsia had no thought of opposing, still less of attempting to end, the regime. They all kept strictly within the limits of Reform Communism, even one as embittered as Solzhenitsyn. All that they wanted was the “truth” about the past. Yet it was inevitable that this prosaic, empirical truth—if pushed far enough—would demolish that Lie which was the system as a whole. The guardians of orthodoxy, such as the Central Committee’s secretary for ideology, Mikhail Suslov, immediately understood this and undertook to whip up a backlash. A month after the publication of

, Khrushchev was inveigled into visiting an exhibition of abstract painting, which caused him to explode with a barrage of expletives and to comment that “a donkey could do better with its tail.” And so the rollback began: Solzhenitsyn got to publish only two more stories in Russia, and the Gulag ceased to be a subject for literature. Nonetheless, the damage to the system’s credibility could no more be undone than could the damage to the “cult” after the Twentieth Congress. With the great thaw following the Twenty-second Congress, and with his restructuring of the Party, Khrushchev had inadvertently begun the long process of subverting Communism by attempting to reform it.

zh: 自取败局
en: RIDING FOR A FALL

zh: 赫鲁晓夫通过其外交政策冒险，取得了同样矛盾的结果。他继承的是一个看似统一、列阵对抗美国“帝国主义”的国际共产主义运动；而他留下的是一个分裂的运动，以及一个被对手超级大国羞辱的苏联国家。斯大林最后几年共产主义那看似不可阻挡的前进势头，已陷入一场将持续四分之一世纪的全球阵地战。赫鲁晓夫执政初期似乎正在走向结束的冷战，到他执政末期仍在继续。
en: Khrushchev achieved similarly contradictory results through his adventures in foreign policy. He inherited a seemingly unified international Communist movement arrayed against American “imperial-ism,” and he left a divided movement with his own Soviet state humiliated by the rival superpower. The seemingly irresistible forward momentum of Communism during the last years of Stalin had bogged down in a global war of positions that would last for the next quarter century. The Cold War that had appeared to be drawing to a close early in Khrushchev’s reign was still very much an ongoing affair by its end.

zh: 赫鲁晓夫时期苏联外交政策的中心关切，本质上与斯大林时期相同：取得国际安全，使苏联国家能够发展其全球力量。而赫鲁晓夫追求这一目标的方法也与斯大林有相似之处：以咄咄逼人的尚武姿态恫吓对手，同时又有失控的倾向。
en: The central concern of Soviet foreign policy under Khrushchev was essentially what it had been under Stalin: international security that would permit the Soviet state to develop its global power. And Khrushchev’s method of pursuing this end also showed similarities to Stalin’s: an intimidatingly militant bluster with a tendency to get out of control.

zh: 恫吓的一部分，是在第三世界推行新的积极推进政策。那是斯大林从未渗入的地区，而赫鲁晓夫利用战后非殖民化，在印度、近东和非洲活跃起来；他为比莱钢铁厂提供资金，协助建设纳赛尔时期的阿斯旺大坝，并支持刚果的帕特里斯·卢蒙巴。这一切令西方大为不安，因为它似乎赋予共产主义以新的、扩展的势头。事实上，它确实提升了苏联作为强国的威望，以及社会主义作为社会模式的威望。但它花费了大量金钱，却没有给莫斯科带来具体的经济收益。
en: A part of the bluster was a new forward policy in the Third World, an area Stalin had never penetrated, Khrushchev, taking advantage of postwar decolonization, became active in India, the Near East, and Africa; he financed Nehru’s steelworks at Bhilai, built Nasser’s Aswan Dam, and supported Patrice Lumumba in the Congo. All of this disturbed the West greatly, for it seemed to give Communism a renewed and extended momentum. And in fact it did serve to enhance the prestige of the Soviet Union as a power, and of socialism as a model of society. Still, it cost a great deal of money and brought Moscow no concrete economic gain.

zh: 但赫鲁晓夫在国际上首要关注的对象是美国、德国和中国，因为对苏联安全的威胁只能来自这些方向。

而且，这三个关切相互关联，并且都与核武器问题相联系。简而言之，苏联政策的主要目标，是在同美国实现核均势的同时，让中国和德国保持无核且弱小。德国人只有在美国人允许的情况下才能获得核武器，因此让德国保持弱小的办法，是与华盛顿达成某种交易。但让中国保持无核要棘手得多，因为中国是一个受到美帝国主义威胁的盟友。与华盛顿达成交易会疏远这个盟友，而过于积极地保卫这个盟友又会妨碍与华盛顿达成交易。于是赫鲁晓夫最终两头落空，从而造成了他本人以及国际共产主义的第一次重大失败。
en: But the primary objects of international concern to Khrushchev were the United States, Germany, and China, because a threat to Soviet security could come only from these quarters.

The three concerns, moreover, were interrelated, and all were linked to the problem of nuclear weapons. In brief, the chief aim of Soviet policy was to achieve nuclear parity with the United States while keeping China and Germany nonnuclear and weak. The Germans could acquire nuclear weapons only if the Americans permitted it, so the way to keep Germany weak was by some sort of deal with Washington. But keeping the Chinese nonnuclear was much trickier because they were an ally under threat from American imperialism. A deal with Washington would alienate this ally, and too active a defense of the ally would preclude a deal with Washington. So Khrushchev eventually fell between these two stools, thereby producing his, and international Communism’s, first major defeat.

zh: 这个问题的根源在于，中国是一个与苏联接壤的庞大国家；这一事实使它成为天然的对手，而不是天然的盟友。因此，两国之间的同盟首先是意识形态的产物，也是双方都需要社会主义神话作为合法性力量的产物。但“社会主义阵营牢不可破的统一”这一神话绝非小事，因为共产主义如同古代教会，必须是普世的，才能被视为真理。它的普世性是它“科学基础”的第一项证明，而它的统一则是它必将战无不胜、其征服不可逆转的主要保证。因此，国际运动的任何分裂，都会威胁其可信性及其在各地对权力的掌控。铁托的叛离以及另一种与之竞争的共产主义形式的创立已经够糟了；在中国这样的规模上重演这一幕，将是一场灾难。然而，形势不可阻挡地把赫鲁晓夫推向了这样一场致命的分裂。
en: The root of this problem was China’s very existence as a huge country bordering the Soviet Union; that fact made it a natural rival, not a natural ally. Thus the alliance between the two countries was above all the product of ideology and a shared need for the socialist mystique as a legitimizing force. But the myth of the “unshakable unity of the socialist camp” was no small matter, for Communism, like the ancient Church, must be catholic if it is to be deemed true. Its universality is the first proof of its “scientific foundation,” and its unity is the main guarantee that it will prove invincible and its conquests irrevocable. Any fragmenting of the international movement, therefore, threatens its credibility and its hold on power everywhere. The defection of Tito and the creation of a rival form of Communism had been bad enough; a repetition of this on the scale of China would be a disaster. Yet circumstances inexorably pushed Khrushchev into such a fatal schism.

zh: 第一个情况是，中国太大，不可能不要求在指导国际运动方面与苏联平等，而苏联若放弃最高领导地位，就会被削弱。第二个情况是，1950年代的中国卷入了与美国的深刻冲突，而美国仍在保护台湾的国民党政权。中国人以共产主义团结的名义，要求苏联在反抗美国、夺取该岛时给予全力支持，甚至包括核武器，而苏联人则躲躲闪闪地按兵不动。一方面，苏联需要中国同盟和阵营的统一，以加强自己同美国打交道的地位。另一方面，苏联人害怕中国的战斗精神可能把他们拖入与美国的战争——尤其是因为毛泽东开始轻描淡写地宣称，在一场核冲突中损失三亿中国人是可以接受的，因为中国还可以用剩下的三亿人建设社会主义。苏联领导人一直维持这种平衡，直到1959年，他们终于断然拒绝帮助中国制造原子弹，并逐步减少了对民用核能项目的援助。
en: The first circumstance was that China was too big not to demand equality with the Soviet Union in directing the international movement, while the Soviet Union would be diminished if it abandoned paramount leadership. The second circumstance was that China in the 1950s was embroiled in a deep conflict with the United States, which was still protecting the nationalist regime in Taiwan. In the name of Communist solidarity, the Chinese demanded all-out Soviet support, including even nuclear weapons, in defying the United States and taking the island, while the Soviets held back evasively. On the one hand, the Soviets needed the Chinese alliance and the unity of the bloc to strengthen their own position in dealing with the United States. On the other hand, the Soviets were afraid that Chinese militancy might draw them into war with the United States—especially since Mao had taken to making blithe declarations about the acceptability of losing three hundred million of his people in a nuclear conflict, because China could still build socialism with the three hundred million that would remain. Soviet leaders continued this balancing act until 1959, when at last they flatly refused to help China build a bomb and wound down their aid for civilian nuclear energy.

zh: 与此同时，中国人放弃了此前一直遵循的苏联社会主义建设模式，随着1958年的大跃进，开始狂热地寻找自己的“通往社会主义的单独道路”。这一纲领让人想起斯大林1929年的自上而下的革命，或列宁1918年的战时共产主义。但它声称要超越任何苏联先例，跳过仅按不平等标准给劳动者报酬的社会主义，进入绝对平等的完整共产主义。这要通过回归中国内战的游击精神来实现，但这种精神现在将被用于建立巨大的“人民公社”，以及在农民后院土高炉里炼钢。借助这场大跃进，中国本应成为一个能够独自反抗美国的强大工业国，而整个运动是在台湾海峡危机的高潮中展开的。这一纲领还要成为所有第三世界的殖民地国家的榜样和磁石，包括曾对法国进行“民族解放战争”的越南。因此，中国的新路线既针对西方帝国主义，也针对苏联对世界共产主义运动的领导权。
en: Concurrently, the Chinese abandoned the Soviet model of building socialism, which they had hitherto followed, and embarked on a frenetic quest for their own “separate road to socialism” with the Great Leap Forward of 1958. This program was reminiscent of Stalin’s revolution from above of 1929, or of Lenin’s War Communism of 1918. But it purported to go beyond any Soviet precedent and to skip over mere socialism—where workers are rewarded unequally—into the full Communism of absolute equality. This was to be achieved by a return to the guerrilla ethos of the Chinese Civil War, but it would now be applied to the creation of gigantic “people’s communes” and to the production of steel in backyard peasant foundries. With this Great Leap, China was supposed to become a mighty industrial power capable of defying the Americans on its own, and the whole campaign unfolded at the height of the crisis in the Taiwan Straits. This program was also to serve as a model and a magnet for all colonial Third World countries, including Vietnam, which had engaged in a “war of national liberation” against France. China’s new course was thus directed against both Western imperialism and Soviet leadership of the world Communist movement.

zh: 尽管中国的纲领以灾难告终并不得不放弃——约三千万人死于饥荒——但它留下了重要的政治遗产。从此以后，中国是世界共产主义中的战斗力量，毛泽东是资深革命领袖，而赫鲁晓夫治下（以及后来勃列日涅夫治下）的苏联则是“富人”或“白人”的伪社会主义，长期倾向于同帝国主义妥协。于是，除了铁托的自我管理之外，又有了另一种社会主义模式与最初的苏联版本竞争；而这两个异端模式对从东南亚到非洲的整个第三世界国家和“人民运动”都具有真正的吸引力。由此产生的两个共产主义巨人之间的紧张如此之大，以至于1962年赫鲁晓夫撤走了所有在华苏联顾问和信贷，从此两个大国之间的实际合作停止。
en: Although China’s program ended in disaster and had to be abandoned—some thirty million people perished from famine—it left an important political legacy. Henceforth China was the militant force in world Communism, and Mao the senior revolutionary leader, whereas the Soviet Union under Khrushchev (and later under Brezhnev) was the “rich man’s” or the “white man’s” pseudosocialism, chronically inclined to compromise with imperialism. Thus another model of socialism, alongside Tito’s self-management, now competed with the original Soviet version, And these two heretical models held real attraction for countries and “people’s movements” throughout the Third World, from Southeast Asia to Africa. The resulting tension between the two Communist giants was so great that in 1962 Khrushchev withdrew all Soviet advisors and credits from China, and from this time onward practical collaboration between the two powers ceased.

zh: 尽管如此，双方都仍需以社会主义阵营来界定自己，这使争端在更长一段时间内基本躲过了“帝国主义者”的眼睛；而这一情况在很大程度上促使美国介入了第二次越南战争。但社会主义阵营的神话也使苏联和中国都相信，一旦对方回头——对中国人来说也许是赫鲁晓夫下台之后，对苏联人来说也许是毛泽东去世之后——统一终将恢复。因此，实际决裂之后，是一场漫长的意识形态争吵，围绕“教条主义”与“修正主义”、“走资派”与“新斯大林主义者”，或围绕赫鲁晓夫1961年新党纲、铁托1957年新纲领的错误。直到1964年，中国才公开谴责苏联不再是一个社会主义国家，而事实上是一个“帝国主义”强国。此后，莫斯科一再试图召开世界共产党代表大会的努力都将徒劳无功。但直到1972年尼克松总统访华，社会主义阵营的神话才最终死去。
en: Still, the need of each party to define itself in terms of the socialist camp kept the dispute largely concealed from the eyes of the “imperialists” for some time longer; and this circumstance had a lot to do with prompting American intervention in the second Vietnam War. But the myth of the socialist camp also led both the Soviet Union and China to believe that unity would someday be restored once the other side recanted—perhaps after the fall of Khrushchev for the Chinese, or of Mao for the Soviets. So the actual break was followed by a long ideological wrangle over “dogmatism” and “revisionism,” “capitalist roaders” and “neo-Stalinists,” or over the errors of Khrushchev’s new Party Program of 1961, or of Tito’s New Program of 1957. It was not until 1964 that the Chinese openly denounced the Soviet Union as being no longer a socialist country but in fact an “imperialist” power. After this, Moscow’s recurrent efforts to convene a world congress of Communist parties would prove futile. But it was not until President Nixon’s visit to China in 1972 that the myth of a socialist camp finally died.

zh: 就真实的国际力量而言，苏联人从这场决裂中损失不大：1950年代“中苏集团”中六亿中国人的支持，历来更多提供的是力量的表象而非实质。尽管如此，在一个合法性来自唯一不可抗拒的意识形态的制度中，这种分裂代表着可信性的损失，而可信性的损失最终会转化为权力的损失。而这种损失将首先在国内感受到。与中国的决裂发生在去斯大林化之后，进一步削弱了政权关于自己掌握唯一真传、为通往完整共产主义“光辉未来”铺路的说法。而中苏利益的公开冲突——它在1969年导致黑龙江上的短暂武装冲突——削弱了列宁主义的一个命题：只有帝国主义才孕育战争，而社会主义孕育和平。
en: In terms of real international power, the Soviets lost little from this break: the support of six hundred million Chinese in the “Sino-Soviet bloc” during the 1950s had always provided more the appearance than the reality of strength. Still, in a system whose legitimacy derived from a single irresistible ideology, this schism represented a loss of credibility that would eventually translate into a loss of power. And this loss would be felt first at home. The break with China, coming in the wake of de-Stalinization, diminished still further the regime’s claim that it held the one true teaching for preparing the way to the “radiant future” of full communism. And the open conflict of Chinese and Soviet interests—which led to a brief armed clash on the Amur River in 1969—undermined the Leninist proposition that only imperialism spawned war, whereas socialism bred peace.

zh: 从某种意义上说，赫鲁晓夫“失去了中国”，是因为他希望对美国和德国获得安全。
他与美国的问题在于，在整个这一时期，美国在核军备方面都处于优势地位，而他想找到某种办法取得表面上的均势。他与德国的问题在于，德国已经重新武装并被纳入北约，而他想阻止这一进程达到核层次。解决这两个问题的办法，都是与华盛顿达成妥协。但赫鲁晓夫寻求这种妥协的方法包含着大量虚张声势和唬骗，事实上危险地违背了他所期望的目的。
en: In a sense Khrushchev “lost China” because he hoped to gain security vis-à-vis the United States and Germany.

His problem with the United States was that throughout this period it was in a position of superiority with regard to nuclear armaments, and he wished to find some means of achieving a semblance of parity. His problem with Germany was that it had been rearmed and taken into NATO, and he wished to prevent this process from reaching the nuclear level. The way to solve both problems was through an accommodation with Washington. But Khrushchev’s method of seeking such accommodation involved a large measure of bluster and bluff, which in fact worked dangerously against his desired end.

zh: 苏联的核计划和弹道导弹计划，如同成熟制度中的其他一切，都是在斯大林治下启动的。然而，他的继承人基本上不熟悉这两项计划，因此不得不自行制定战略。

他们的问题有两方面。第一，在1953年热核突破之后，他们的原子弹和弹头产量远低于美国。第二，苏联无法生产一支能与美国战略空军司令部所辖机队相比的远程轰炸机队来投送核武器。赫鲁晓夫对这两个问题的解决办法，被称为“战略欺骗”。他们在大气层中进行超级炸弹的壮观试验，以给人拥有庞大武库的印象。与此同时，苏联利用人造卫星和其他导弹发射的成功，造成一种拥有足以抵消美国远程轰炸机优势的洲际弹道导弹（ICBM）能力的印象。这两种欺骗都依赖保密，因为直到1950年代末，美国还没有足够的手段从空中侦测苏联军事设施。于是赫鲁晓夫利用力量的表象，试图胁迫华盛顿达成一项全球性的共同安全交易。
en: The Soviet nuclear and ballistic missile programs, like everything else in the mature system, had been launched under Stalin. His heirs, however, were largely unacquainted with either program and thus had to develop a strategy on their own.

Their problem was twofold. First, their production of bombs and warheads after the thermonuclear breakthrough of 1953 was well below that of the United States. Second, the Soviet Union could not produce a fleet of long-range bombers comparable to those of the American Strategic Air Command to deliver nuclear weapons. Khrushchev’s solution to both problems has been called “strategic deception.” Spectacular tests of superbombs were conducted in the atmosphere to give the impression of possessing a huge arsenal. At the same time, Soviet successes with Sputnik and other missile launchings were exploited to give the impression of an intercontinental ballistic missile (ICBM) capability sufficient to counteract America’s superiority in long-range bombers. Both of these deceptions depended on secrecy, since until late in the 1950s the United States had no adequate means of aerial detection of Soviet military installations. So Khrushchev used the appearance of strength to attempt to intimidate Washington into a global deal for mutual security.

zh: 这笔交易的核心是：如果美国人接受一个中立、无核的德国以及同苏联的军事均势，莫斯科就让中国保持无核。这当然从未被明确说出，而是通过政治压力和外交手腕传递出来。通过1956—1958年的火箭恫吓和核试验，赫鲁晓夫寻求并获得了1959年访美的邀请，以及1960年在巴黎举行四国峰会的安排，两者都是解决德国问题的前奏。为了进一步推动这一进程，1958年他在柏林问题上向华盛顿发出了近乎最后通牒的要求：必须在六个月内签订对德和约，否则莫斯科将单独与东德缔约，从而把通往柏林的通道移交给这个新国家。然而，这样做与其说是要把盟国挤出柏林，不如说是要制造一个筹码，促使他们放弃重新武装西德。当这一威胁没有产生预期结果时，赫鲁晓夫还是去了戴维营（随后立即赶往北京安抚愤怒的中国盟友），但柏林问题仍然是对西方施压的手段，甚至在1961年修建柏林墙之后依然如此。
en: The essence of the deal was that Moscow would keep China non-nuclear if the Americans would accept a neutral and nonnuclear Germany as well as military parity with the Soviet Union. This, of course, was never stated in so many words, but was telegraphed by political pressure and diplomatic maneuver. Through rocket rattling and bomb testing during 1956-1958, Khrushchev sought and achieved his invitation to the United States in 1959 and the scheduling of a four-power summit in Paris in 1960, both as a prelude to a settlement of the German problem. To give further impetus to this process, in 1958 he gave Washington what sounded like an ultimatum over Berlin: a German peace treaty was to be signed within six months or Moscow would make one separately with East Germany, thereby turning over access routes to Berlin to the new state. The purpose of this, however, was not so much to squeeze the allies out of Berlin as to create a bargaining chip for getting them to abandon the rearming of West Germany. When this threat did not produce the desired results. Khrushchev went to Camp David anyway (and then immediately rushed to Peking to appease his irate Chinese allies), but the Berlin issue remained as a goad to the West, even after the construction of the Wall in 1961.

zh: 这种平衡术似乎一直运作得相当顺利，直到1960年骗局被识破，恫吓导致了重大危机。1950年代末，美国U-2间谍飞机的越境侦察已经揭示，苏联并不具备其试验和吹嘘所暗示的洲际弹道导弹能力。随后在1960年，一架U-2在斯维尔德洛夫斯克上空被击落，而当艾森豪威尔总统拒绝道歉时，赫鲁晓夫突然取消了已聚集各方领导人的巴黎峰会，以维护自己在国内和北京的地位。1961年，他在维也纳与肯尼迪总统会晤时再次加大柏林问题上的压力；肯尼迪刚刚因入侵古巴的猪湾惨败而在国际上受挫，而同年晚些时候柏林墙的修建又进一步加大了这种压力。
en: This balancing act seemed to be working well enough until 1960, when the deception was found out and intimidation led to major crisis. In the late 1950s overflights by the American U-2 spy plane had revealed that the Soviets did not have the ICBM capability suggested by their testing and boasting. Then, in 1960, a U-2 was shot down over Sverdlovsk, and when President Eisenhower refused to apologize, Khrushchev abruptly cancelled the already assembled Paris summit to cover his position both at home and in Peking. In 1961 he stepped up the pressure again over Berlin at a meeting in Vienna with President Kennedy, who had just been weakened internationally by the fiasco of the Bay of Pigs invasion of Cuba, a pressure increased still further by the construction of the Berlin Wall later that year.

〔译注〕美国自1956年起使用U-2侦察苏联，但在1960年停止飞越之前并未找到洲际导弹基地；其后“科罗娜”卫星影像对判断苏联导弹部署规模起了重要作用。

zh: 这一切最终导致了恫吓的终极手段：1962年在古巴部署苏联导弹和核弹头。这一举动并非像赫鲁晓夫后来所称的那样，主要是为了保卫古巴免受另一场美国支持的入侵。它是一场疯狂的赌博，是企图以低成本一举解决苏联所有外交问题的绝望努力。第一，它是弥补苏联缺乏洲际弹道导弹的快捷方式：把中程和中远程导弹运到美国的家门口，赫鲁晓夫希望通过地理上的接近实现战略均势。第二，它是安抚苏联军方的一种方式，因为军方的编制和预算已被削减，以支持赫鲁晓夫面向消费者的国内计划。第三，它是一种迫使美国最终接受苏联在柏林和德国问题上的立场的方式，也许还可以把古巴的导弹当作真正的筹码。最后，它是一种向中国表明俄国没有对帝国主义软下来、因此中国人不需要自己拥有原子弹的方式。
en: All of this culminated in the ultimate measure of intimidation, the placement of Soviet missiles and nuclear warheads in Cuba in 1962. This move was not undertaken primarily to defend Cuba against another American-sponsored invasion, as Khrushchev later alleged. It was, rather, a wild wager, a desperate effort to solve all of the Soviet Union’s foreign problems on the cheap. It was, first, a quick way to make up for the Soviets’ lack of ICBMs: By moving medium- and intermediate-range missiles to the United States’ doorstep, Khrushchev hoped to achieve strategic parity through geographic proximity. Second, it was a way to appease the Soviet military, whose effectives and budgets had been cut back in favor of Khrushchev’s domestic programs for consumers. And third, it was a way to force America to accept at last the Soviet position on Berlin and Germany, perhaps by using the missiles in Cuba as an actual bargaining chip. Finally, it was a way to show the Chinese that Russia had not gone soft on imperialism and that they therefore did not need a bomb of their own.

zh: 然而，要实现这些目标中的任何一个或全部，赫鲁晓夫都必须在自己选定的时刻戏剧性地公开苏联导弹的存在，然后就其要求发起峰会谈判。这无疑正是他的意图。但在他尚未在古巴完全布置好之前，一架美国U-2侦察机就发现了导弹——而他本应在开始之前就知道这很有可能。该岛随后被美军“隔离”；他的虚张声势被戳穿；他不得不退让，除了肯尼迪口头上的让步之外一无所获。整个战后时期最严重的危机就这样结束了。
en: To achieve any or all of these objectives, however, Khrushchev would have had to dramatically reveal the presence of the Soviet missiles at the moment of his own choosing and then initiate summit negotiations on his demands. And this was no doubt his intention. But an American U-2 found him out before he had fully set up shop on Cuba, as indeed he should have known was likely before he started. The island was then “quarantined” by American forces; his bluff was called; and he had to back down, having gained no more than verbal concessions from Kennedy. Thus ended the gravest crisis of the whole postwar period.

〔译注〕危机的公开安排包括美国不入侵古巴的承诺；美国还通过秘密渠道同意撤走土耳其的朱庇特导弹，并于次年实施，不能说苏联只得到口头让步。

zh: 矛盾的是，它发生在冷战总体上正在消退的时刻。禁止核试验的谈判早在1959年就已开始，而禁止在大气层进行试验的条约在危机后不久的1963年签署，从而开启了将持续到1990年的漫长军备限制与谈判进程。1963年还发生了美国首次向苏联出售粮食，从而开启了另一个长期进程。尽管如此，古巴导弹危机虽然是个例外，却并非仅仅由赫鲁晓夫冲动的个性造成的偶然事件。它也是苏联国际地位根本弱点的表现：由于他们的制度实际上无法为其超级大国地位提供资源，用某种轻率权宜之计弥补这一弱点的诱惑始终存在。赫鲁晓夫的古巴赌博只是其中最引人注目的案例。朝鲜是较早的例子。后来还会有别的例子。
en: Paradoxically, it occurred at a moment when the Cold War was generally on the wane. Negotiations for a nuclear test ban had already begun in 1959, and the treaty outlawing testing in the atmosphere was signed shortly after the crisis, in 1963, thereby inaugurating the long process of arms limitation and negotiations that would continue until 1990. The year 1963 also saw the first American grain sale to the Soviets, thus beginning another long-term process. Still, the Cuban missile crisis, though an exception, was not a fluke due solely to the impetuous personality of Khrushchev. It was also the expression of a fundamental weakness in the Soviets’ international position: because their system did not really provide the resources for their superpower status, the temptation was always present to make up for this weakness by some rash expedient. Khrushchev’s Cuban gamble was only the most spectacular case of this. Korea had been an earlier example. And there would be other instances later.

zh: 1962年导弹危机的另一个矛盾之处在于，它只在西方被视为一场危机。苏联民众直到危机结束都不知道出了什么事，即便在那之后，多数人也不明白那个时刻有多危险。这是因为政权向民众呈现的世界图景是：苏联虽然受到帝国主义攻击，却仍然不可战胜。冷战和军备竞赛被呈现为西方单方面针对苏联的威胁，而“争取和平的斗争”则被宣称是苏联政策的决定性特征。在这种氛围中，结束冷战和限制军备竞赛从来不是苏联民众普遍关心的问题，尽管这些事业在西方却是重要群体的重大议题。苏联民众的关切压倒性地是国内问题——从改善生活水平到减少镇压。苏联没有“和平运动”，这一情况使赫鲁晓夫在外交政策上拥有完全自由的行动空间。因此，他可以一头跳进古巴，而除了党的领导层之外不对任何人负责。
en: Another paradox of the 1962 missile crisis is that it was perceived as a crisis only in the West. The Soviet population did not know that anything was going on until it was over, and even then most did not realize how dangerous the moment had been. This is because the regime presented the population with a picture of the world in which the Soviet Union, although assailed by imperialism, was nonetheless invincible. The Cold War and the arms race were presented as threats unilaterally directed by the West against the Soviet Union, while the “struggle for peace” was claimed as the defining characteristic of Soviet policy. In this atmosphere, ending the Cold War and curtailing the arms race were never a widespread concern among the Soviet population, even though these causes were a major issue to important groups in the West. The Soviet population’s concerns were overwhelmingly domestic—from improving living standards to curtailing repression. There was no “peace movement” in the Soviet Union, and this circumstance gave Khrushchev a completely free hand for a bold foreign policy. Thus he could leap into Cuba accountable to no one but the Party leadership.

zh: 但在同僚们看来，尽管肯尼迪尽可能让他保全面子，赫鲁晓夫作为领袖的可信性此时已严重受损。此外，古巴的失败发生的同时，还有他批准出版《伊凡·杰尼索维奇》的“错误”，以及他决定把党一分为二。1962年秋天的这三件事加在一起，构成了赫鲁晓夫1964年10月被解除职务的最早几项原因。
en: But in the eyes of his colleagues, even though Kennedy let him save as much face as possible, Khrushchev’s credibility as leader was now seriously damaged. Moreover, the defeat in Cuba occurred at the same time as his “error” in authorizing the publication of
and his decision to split the Party in two. These three events of the autumn of 1962, taken together, constitute the first reasons for Khrushchev’s removal from power in October 1964.

zh: 然而，他倒台的一个更根本原因，在于斯大林之后时期党国性质的变化。党本身已不同于十一年前，它与领袖的关系也已不同。
en: An even more fundamental cause of his demise lies in the changed nature of the Party-state in the post-Stalin period. The Party itself was different from what it had been eleven years earlier, and its relationship to the leader was different as well.

zh: 斯大林去世时，党有690万党员，而且正如我们所见，它正稳步成为一个官名录党，一个由此时已成帝国的国家的管理精英主导的党。然而，党新的社团性质仍被掩盖着，因为这个组织完全屈从于斯大林，并受安全警察的监护。到赫鲁晓夫倒台时，党已有1175万党员，并完全成为一个官名录党，即管理精英的团体组织。与此同时，随着贝利亚的倒台，它从警察的监护下解放出来，而事实证明，也从其领袖的掌控下解放出来。但这一点花了十年才变得明显。
en: At Stalin’s death the Party numbered 6.9 million and, as we have seen, was well on its way to becoming a

Party, one dominated by the managerial elite of a now imperial state. The new corporate nature of the Party was still obscured, however, by that organization’s complete subordination to Stalin and by the tutelage of the security police. By the time of Khrushchev’s fall, the Party numbered 11,750,000 and had fully become a

Party, the corporate organization of the managerial elite. At the same time, with Beria’s fall, it was emancipated from police tutelage and, as it turned out, from its leader as well. Yet it took a decade for this to become apparent.

zh: 在1950年代末的鼎盛时期，赫鲁晓夫试图振兴党，就像他试图震动其他一切一样。在这一领域，他的政策同样是民粹主义的，这又是他原初列宁主义的反映。在1956年至1964年间吸收的450万新党员中，入党时是工人的比例越来越高，农民所占比例也有上升，但程度较小；这两类人合计约占50%——这明显逆转了斯大林最后几年越来越多从“知识分子”即管理阶级中吸收党员的趋向。
en: During his prime years at the end of the 1950s, Khrushchev tried to rejuvenate the Party just as he tried to shake up everything else. And in this domain, too, his policy was populist, another reflection of his paleo-Leninism. Of the 4.5 million new members taken in between 1956 and 1964, an increasing percentage were workers and, to a lesser degree, peasants at the time of their enrollment; the two categories together accounted for about 50 percent—a clear reversal of the growing trend of the last years of Stalin to recruit from the “intelligentsia,” that is, the managerial class.

zh: 这一演变与赫鲁晓夫的教育政策相一致。斯大林一旦把自己的制度建立起来，就通过征收学费限制接受高等教育的机会，从而调节新干部进入管理和机关职位的数量；这当然倾向于把干部变成一个种姓。赫鲁晓夫试图通过取消高等教育学费、普及十年制基础学校，使教育民主化。他还试图通过给基础课程增加两年、要求高年级学生一半时间参加经济劳动，使改革后的制度更贴近人民，从而有望防止专业知识分子与群众分离。因此，这项改革是赫鲁晓夫“向共产主义过渡”和“全民国家”的一部分。然而，这一方案违背了日益专业化和分层化的劳动力的本性：改革激怒了希望子女全日在校学习的、向上流动的干部家庭，而把半工半读的劳动者塞进经济又打乱了生产。改革也没有减缓该国社会分化的增长。
en: This evolution was of a piece with Khrushchev’s education policy. Once Stalin had put his system in place, he restricted access to higher education by imposing tuition, thereby regulating the flow of new cadres into managerial and apparat positions; this, of course, tended to make the cadres into a caste. Khrushchev sought to democratize education by abolishing tuition for higher education and by making the basic ten-year school universal. And he attempted to bring the reformed system even closer to the people by adding two years to the basic curriculum and requiring all students in the higher classes to work half-time in the economy, thereby hopefully preventing the separation of a professional intelligentsia from the masses. As such, this reform was a part of Khrushchev’s “transition to communism” and “the state of all the people.” This scheme, however, went against the grain of an increasingly specialized and stratified labor force: the reform irritated the upwardly mobile families of cadres who wished their children to remain full-time in school, while the insertion of part-time workers into the economy disorganized production. Nor did the reform slow down the growth of social differentiation in the country.

zh: 结果是，赫鲁晓夫大幅扩张的党，比斯大林的党更是一个管理精英的组织。以工人身份入党的成员迅速升到低级管理职位。而且受过高等教育的党员人数不断增加。同样重要的是，工人阶级中只有约4%在党内，而被归类为知识分子的人中则有25%是党员。任何希望在制度中获得负有责任的职位的人，都必须最迟在三十出头入党。因此总的来说，到赫鲁晓夫统治末期，党已成为干部名录既得利益集团不受约束的团体组织。
en: The upshot was that Khrushchev’s greatly expanded Party was even more an organization of the managerial elite than Stalin’s Party. Members who entered as workers quickly moved up to minor managerial positions. And a constantly increasing number of members had higher education. Just as important, only around 4 percent of the working class were in the Party, whereas 25 percent of those classified as intelligentsia were members. And anyone who aspired to a position of responsibility in the system had to join the Party in his or her early thirties at the latest. Thus, overall, the Party by the end of Khrushchev’s reign had become the unfettered corporate organization of the
establishment.

zh: 而这个既得利益集团，尤其是其核心的全职党务官僚，不喜欢被投入一场又一场运动，重组之后又重组。它想要稳定，想要安稳地享受自己的权力和特权。
en: And this establishment, especially its inner core of full-time Party apparatchiki, did not like to be thrown into one campaign after another, reorganized and then again reorganized. It wanted stability and the quiet enjoyment of its power and perquisites.

zh: 它也不再那么害怕了。自贝利亚及其主要助手被处决以来，没有任何显要人物因政治原因受到极刑。反党集团的成员——毕竟，他们曾试图发动政变——只是被降职到较次要的工作，而赫鲁晓夫甚至直到1960年才把莫洛托夫及其同伙开除出党。因此，他显然受到同僚的抵制；对他们来说，去斯大林化首先意味着保护党不受
第一书记权力的侵害。而赫鲁晓夫未能清除该集团，是软弱的一个明显迹象，几乎可以保证，未来的某个集团再尝试政变也不会太危险。
en: Nor was it any longer very afraid. Since the execution of Beria and his chief aides, no prominent figure had paid the supreme penalty for political reasons. The members of the Anti-Party Group—which, after all, had attempted a coup d’état—were only demoted to lesser jobs, and Khrushchev was not even able to expel Molotov and company from the Party until 1960. He was thus clearly being resisted by his colleagues, for whom de-Stalinization meant first of all protection of the Party against the power of
First Secretary. And Khrushchev’s failure to eliminate the Group was a patent sign of weakness that almost guaranteed it would not be too dangerous for some future grouping to try a coup again.

zh: 此外，赫鲁晓夫尽管作为第一书记十分活跃，却只是一个“老板”，而不是“领袖”（
）。他从未获得共产主义最高领袖——列宁、斯大林、毛泽东、胡志明、铁托或卡斯特罗——那种魅力型地位，而这种地位只有通过重大革命成就才能获得。到了七十岁，他越来越显得像是党更简单时代的一个不合时宜的旧时代人物。
en: Moreover, Khrushchev, for all his activism as First Secretary, was only a Boss, not a Leader, or

. He never attained the charismatic stature of the supreme Communist chiefs—Lenin, Stalin, Mao, Ho, Tito, or Castro—a stature conferred only by major revolutionary accomplishment. And at seventy years of age, he appeared increasingly as an anachronistic throwback to a simpler era of the Party.

zh: 于是，1964年10月，他在主席团的同僚们作为官名录党的最高守护者，组织了一场成功的政变，让他退休。他们没有给他任何机会去召集他昔日在中央委员会中的省级支持者，何况他早已因分裂党而疏远了这些人。而由于他不再拥有恐吓同僚的警察权力，他别无选择，只能投降。官方说法是，他因健康原因退休。他倒台后，被指责“唯意志论”“主观主义”和制定“异想天开的计划”，所指的就是上文讨论的一连串改革政策。苏联从斯大林主义顶峰痛苦下行的进程中，改革共产主义的第一个大周期就这样结束了。
en: Thus in October 1964 his colleagues in the Presidium, acting as the supreme guardians of the

Party, organized a successful coup and retired him. They left no possibility of summoning his one-time provincial supporters in the Central Committee, whom he had alienated anyway by dividing the Party. And since he no longer possessed the police power to terrorize his colleagues, he had no choice but to capitulate. Officially, he retired for reasons of health. After his fall, he was accused of “voluntarism,” “subjectivism,” and “hare-brained schemes,” by which was meant the cascade of reform policies discussed above. And so ended the first great cycle of Reform Communism in the Soviet Union’s painful descent from its Stalinist peak.
